Mexican officials say the United States flew a surveillance drone over Mexican territory to help locate and capture one of the country's most wanted drug traffickers. The operation led to the arrest of Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, kn
items.text:
US flew surveillance drone over Mexico to help capture top drug lord
Mexican officials say the United States flew a surveillance drone over Mexican territory to help locate and capture one of the country's most wanted drug traffickers. The operation led to the arrest of Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as 'El Chapo Isidro'.
The United States flew a surveillance drone over Mexican territory to help the government track down and capture a top drug lord over the weekend in Sinaloa, Mexican security officials said Monday.
The recent detention of Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro” illustrates increasing law enforcement cooperation between the neighboring countries, but U.S. involvement in Mexican security operations has long been a touchy subject.
U.S. President Donald Trump has pressured Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum to crack down on cartels, while Mexico has repeatedly underscored its sovereignty. On Monday, Sheinbaum emphasized that U.S. forces were not allowed to operate on the ground in Mexico and the governments were only sharing intelligence.
“This case in particular demonstrates the capacity of the armed forces” of Mexico to make major detentions, Sheinbaum said.
The U.S. has sought to line up allies across Latin America to allow them to operate in their territories, with mixed responses from across the region.
The weekend detention of the capo, who was one of the FBI's most wanted fugitives, triggered a burst of violence in the northern state of Sinaloa that left 20 people dead in the city of Guasave. Among them were four soldiers and 16 suspected criminals, Mexican officials said Monday.
Defense Secretary Gen. Ricardo Trevilla Trejo said Monday that the capture of Meza Flores and 16 members of his criminal group was the result of “very important intelligence sharing” with U.S. authorities over the past three months to pinpoint Meza Flores’ location in Guasave.
In the week leading up to Meza Flores’ capture, that included authorizing the U.S. to fly intelligence drones over Mexican territory, to assist Mexican law enforcement to later surround the capo and go in for the capture, Trevilla Trejo and other Mexican officials said. They emphasized that the intelligence mission was carried out in compliance with Mexican law.
Authorities also noted on Monday that the U.S. had an existing extradition request for Meza Flores for drug trafficking charges, leaving open the possibility that the cartel boss may be sent north to face justice.
His capture was celebrated by Mexican and U.S. law enforcement as a major blow to criminal groups in the region.
The U.S. government highlighted its intelligence support in the operation, but did not immediately provide more details about the use of the surveillance drone when asked on Monday.
Meza Flores led the Beltran Leyva organization and later became the leader of his own group, the Meza Flores Transnational Criminal Organization. He was also a key ally of a Sinaloa Cartel faction known as “Los Mayos," which is locked in a brutal territorial war against another cartel faction in the Mexican state.
The capture of Meza Flores was the latest in a string of targeted operations against cartel kingpins by Mexican authorities, the largest of which was the February killing of Jalisco New Generation Cartel leader Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes , known as " El Mencho ."
While the captures show that the government is doubling down on its fight on crime, many experts were quick to emphasize that the strategy could backfire.
In previous anti-crime offensives in Mexico and other parts of Latin America, knocking out cartel leaders without debilitating the entire criminal structure around them has largely only fueled bloody power struggles between cartel factions. That has been the case in recent years in Sinaloa.
(FRANCE 24 with AP)

items.summary:
Appeals court renews Trump bid for federal jurisdiction in hush-money case
Monday’s ruling could clear the way for Trump to argue prosecutors relied on evidence protected by presidential immunity.
A federal appeals court has revived United States President Donald Trump’s bid to transfer his New York
items.text:
Appeals court renews Trump bid for federal jurisdiction in hush-money case
Monday’s ruling could clear the way for Trump to argue prosecutors relied on evidence protected by presidential immunity.
A federal appeals court has revived United States President Donald Trump’s bid to transfer his New York criminal hush-money case to federal court, months after a district judge rejected the effort for a third time.
On Monday, a three-judge panel of the 2nd Circuit Court of Appeals reversed a lower court ruling that had kept the case in New York state court.
In a two-page order, the 2nd Circuit panel said it disagreed with the late US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein’s denial of Trump’s request for the “removal” of his case to federal court.
The appeals court said Hellerstein had “erred in holding that removal is categorically unavailable in a state criminal case” after conviction.
It directed a federal judge in Manhattan to consider whether the proceedings could be brought under federal jurisdiction.
In a written statement provided to The Associated Press news agency, a spokesperson for Trump’s legal team said the president “appreciates the 2nd Circuit’s prompt and correct ruling, as he continues to win against Democrat weaponization of our Justice System”.
Trump has sought to use presidential immunity in federal court to have his conviction overturned. He was convicted on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records in 2024, though he has denied any wrongdoing.
Trump’s New York criminal conviction
The case stems from a $130,000 “hush money” payment made shortly before the 2016 presidential election to adult film performer Stormy Daniels.
Daniels had claimed she had an affair with the Republican leader while he was married — an allegation he denies — and prosecutors alleged that the money was intended to buy her silence during a tense campaign season.
Trump ultimately won the 2016 presidential election, ushering him into his first term in public office.
The payment was made through Trump’s former lawyer and fixer Michael Cohen. Prosecutors argued that Trump fudged his business records to pass off his reimbursements to Cohen as legal expenses, thereby concealing them from voters.
While falsifying business records is normally a misdemeanour offence, it can be charged as a felony if done in service of another crime. In Trump’s case, prosecutors said he violated state election laws.
In May 2024, a New York jury found him guilty, making Trump the first US president to be convicted of a crime.
At a sentencing hearing in January 2025 — shortly before his second term as president began — Trump received an unconditional discharge, meaning he faced neither imprisonment nor a financial penalty. But his conviction remains on the record.
Why does Trump want the case heard in federal court?
For years, Trump has sought to overturn that conviction.
Monday’s ruling leaves the jury’s guilty verdict intact, but it also clears the way for the president to seek a hearing in federal court.
He is expected to argue that state prosecutors secured his conviction by relying on evidence that would have been shielded by presidential immunity in federal court.
His legal team is likely to point to a landmark 2024 ruling as justification for that argument.
At the time, the Supreme Court’s conservative majority ruled that presidents could enjoy “presumptive immunity” for any “official acts” conducted while in office.
What constitutes an “official act”, however, is an open question. Previously, the Supreme Court had only conferred immunity to actions taken within a president’s constitutional authority.
Monday’s ruling reverses a series of setbacks for Trump’s legal team.
In August, federal judge Hellerstein rejected Trump’s third attempt to transfer the case, finding that the president’s arguments were insufficient to justify moving it out of state court.
Hellerstein, a senior federal judge in Manhattan’s Southern District of New York, died last month at the age of 92.
The move also stalls Trump’s state-level appeal in New York’s Appellate Division, which heard arguments earlier this month but has yet to rule on his challenge.
A federal judge has been directed to rule promptly on whether the case should indeed be transferred from New York state court to federal jurisdiction, although no deadline has been set.

items.text:
Israeli minister approves return of Flydubai flights to Tel Aviv
Final resumption of carrier’s route between Dubai and Tel Aviv depends on Israeli security authorities’ approval.
Israeli Transportation Minister Miri Regev has approved the resumption of Flydubai flights to Tel Aviv, according to Israeli media, almost two months after an onboard incident where a co-pilot was accused of attacking his captain.
Regev made the announcement on Monday, though Israel’s security authorities’ approval is still required for flights to resume. The ministry expects operations to resume within a week or two, Israeli media said.
The minister’s approval comes after talks between Israeli officials, led by ministry Director-General Moshe Ben-Zaken, and Emirati aviation officials took place in Dubai on November 16.
Authorities discussed potential security measures that would allow for airlines to fully resume flights between Dubai and Tel Aviv.
“The delegation today presented Regev with the steps the company has taken in the wake of the incident,” Israeli media reported, citing a transportation ministry statement. “As a result, Regev approved the return of Flydubai, subject to clearance from security authorities.”
“The move is a significant step toward restoring air connectivity between Israel and the UAE and expanding flight options for passengers,” the statement added.
Flydubai halted flights to Tel Aviv on September 30 as it began an investigation into the events that transpired on board a Boeing 737 Max 8. Israeli carriers also stopped running routes to Dubai, making Etihad, which flies to Abu Dhabi, the only carrier flying between the UAE and Israel, according to Israeli media.
The co-pilot, who was identified as an Omani national, was arrested when the plane diverted and made an emergency landing in Tabuk, northwestern Saudi Arabia.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accused the co-pilot of trying to crash the plane and of attacking the captain, Smit Machchhar, an Indian national.
The emergency came a day after Netanyahu warned of possible attacks in the lead-up to Israel’s October 27 parliamentary elections.

items.text:
Bukele shares details on deaths of Salvadoran troops in Haiti intervention
Bukele’s military intervention in Haiti comes after four Salvadoran technicians were kidnapped by gangs in October.
Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele has identified the three soldiers from his Central American country who were killed while on an anti-gang mission in Haiti.
Late on Sunday, Bukele posted on social media that their names were Lieutenant Cristian Daniel Palacios Santos and Corporals Emerson Alexander Zepeda Zelada and Wilber Manuel Serrano Medina.
“Tragically, an accidental explosion during that mission claimed their lives,” Bukele said.
He also described instances in which the men had shown “bravery” in the past.
During “tests in El Salvador”, Bukele said that Zepeda Zelada and Serrano Medina took quick action to disarm a grenade lodged in a drone.
“It was not possible to steer the drone toward a completely safe area for it to crash,” Bukele said. “They were fully aware of the immense risk they were taking, yet they chose to act to protect others. And they succeeded.”
According to Bukele, Palacios Santos was admired for recently taking control during a “critical moment” in an operation in which some contractors allegedly retreated.
“He acted with speed and determination, managing to save several lives, including those of his own colleagues,” Bukele wrote. “We all applaud his bravery.”
He didn’t identify the contractors.
Bukele also used his post to pledge that Salvadoran troops who want to leave Haiti could do so immediately without facing reprisals.
Bukele makes a promise to Salvadorans
The Salvadoran soldiers killed last week were among 2,500 deployed to Haiti last month after four of their own went missing during an October 18 attack in gang-held territory. They have not yet been found.
Bukele said that his government would award the families of the three soldiers killed on Friday $200,000 in addition to a monthly income.
He also stressed that any soldier who wants to leave Haiti immediately may do so “without fear of reprisal and without concern that their return might jeopardise the mission, as many of their comrades have volunteered to relieve anyone who wishes to be relieved”.
Salvadoran troops have come under increased scrutiny as experts and the United Nations note they are operating in a largely unilateral way. Thousands of Haitians recently demonstrated to support Bukele.
The agreement between Haiti and El Salvador hasn’t been made public.
“There is no information on the scope and limits of its mission, nor on its accountability mechanisms,” according to a report published Monday by NAL Human Rights, a Netherlands-based consulting company focused on Central American issues.
It noted that, regardless of what that deal stipulates, Salvadoran and international laws require that El Salvador’s armed forces comply with human rights and humanitarian laws.
The report also underscored that the Central American country and the International Criminal Court have jurisdiction to prosecute Salvadoran military personnel if they are accused of war crimes, genocide or crimes against humanity.
More than 20,000 people have been killed in gang-related violence across Haiti in the past five years.
US lawmakers demand answers about the situation in Haiti
The deaths of the Salvadoran soldiers come as local and international forces fight powerful gangs entrenched in Martissant, a community located in a key corridor that links Haiti’s capital to the country’s western and southern regions.
Dozens of suspected gang members have been killed since last week as the battle in Martissant continues, police have said.
It is the first major operation in Martissant in the more than five years that gangs have controlled it.
As Haitian police and others continue to battle gangs in Martissant, a UN-backed gang suppression force said it killed several suspected gang members on Sunday as part of ongoing operations in Tabarre and Cite Soleil, located in Port-au-Prince, and in the northern town of Gros Morne.
As fighting intensifies, two Democratic lawmakers on Monday accused the administration of US President Donald Trump of failing to “name and sanction the political and economic elite fueling Haiti’s insecurity”.
The concern was outlined in a letter penned by New Hampshire Senator Jeanne Shaheen, the ranking member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, and New York Representative Gregory Meeks, the ranking member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee.
“At a time when the Haitian people are preparing to vote for the first time in over a decade, Congress, the American public and the Haitian people deserve transparency about the nature and scale of collusion between gangs and their political and economic support networks,” they said.
The letter was addressed to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.
Haiti is scheduled to hold the first round of elections in July 2027. Among the candidates running are some previously sanctioned by the United States and Canada.

items.title: U.S. to co-host Women's World Cup in 2031; U.K. wins bid for 2035
items.summary:
The United States has been confirmed as co-hosts of the 2031 Women's World Cup, before the United Kingdom will host the tournament four years later.
The FIFA congress on Monday approved a joint bid from Mexico, the United States, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031 World Cup.
The combined bid fr
items.text:
The United States has been confirmed as co-hosts of the 2031 Women's World Cup, before the United Kingdom will host the tournament four years later.
The FIFA congress on Monday approved a joint bid from Mexico, the United States, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031 World Cup.
The combined bid from England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland was the sole bidder for the 2035 competition. To date, 19 venues have been put forward as potential options to host the tournament, with 14 grounds across England, two in Scotland, two in Wales and one in Northern Ireland.
The winning candidates and FIFA president Gianni Infantino promised commercially successful tournaments -- the first editions with 48 teams and 104 games -- and to reinvest all that money in women's soccer.
"This will be the largest women's sporting event in history," the U.S. Soccer Federation president, Cindy Parlow Cone, told FIFA members in a pre-vote presentation at the governing body's headquarters in Zurich. "Which means we have to deliver."
The U.S.-led bid previously predicted tournament revenues of $4 billion, and Parlow Cone said after the FIFA decision that "if we do it right we probably will surpass that."
FIFA wanted these heavyweights of women's soccer to face no opposition without rival bids and host the first expanded tournaments. That will bring parity with the men's World Cup which expanded to 48 teams this year in the U.S., Canada and Mexico.
The 2027 Women's World Cup will have 32 teams in Brazil.
The U.S.-led 2031 project across the Concacaf regional soccer body bid offers FIFA a choice of stadiums in 20 cities: 14 in the U.S., four in Mexico plus San José in Costa Rica and Kingston, Jamaica.
Women's soccer in Jamaica already has a good reputation, with standout forward Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw starring for Manchester City and the national team finishing unbeaten above Brazil in their group at the 2023 World Cup.
Parlow Cone said "we have a responsibility to raise the boats of every country" in women's soccer.
"I know first hand what hosting a Women's World Cup can do, and I wanted the same for throughout our region. It's going to be transformative for us, but imagine what it will do for Jamaica for the 'Reggae Girlz' to play in their home stadium in a World Cup match," Parlow Cone said.
The pair of four-nation co-hosting bids had a clear run in the past 20 months and were approved Monday by acclamation in an online meeting of FIFA's 211 member federations.
The U.S. previously hosted the Women's World Cup alone in 1999 and 2003. The national team's tournament win in 1999 was the second of its four titles.
It will be the first time since 1966 the U.K. has hosted a World Cup. The U.K. will also host the men's European Championships in 2028, but had previously failed in bids to secure the 2006 and 2018 men's World Cups.
The English stadiums included in the bid are: Brighton's Amex, Bristol City's Ashton Gate, Nottingham Forest's City Ground, Leeds United's Elland Road, Arsenal's Emirates Stadium, Manchester City's Etihad Stadium, Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium, Manchester United's Old Trafford, Newcastle United's St James' Park, Crystal Palace's Selhurst Park, Sunderland's Stadium of Light, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Villa Park and Wembley.
Chelsea's potential new stadium, Wrexham's redeveloped ground and Birmingham's new 62,000-capacity Powerhouse Stadium could also be added.
In Wales, the Principality Stadium and Cardiff City Stadium are on the list. A redeveloped Windsor Park in Northern Ireland is also on the list as are Edinburgh's Easter Road and Glasgow's Hampden Park in Scotland.
FIFA's evaluation of the bid gave it a rating of 4.3 out of five, with the contractual framework of the bid rated "medium risk."
FIFA's evaluation said: "The bidder has submitted an extensive set of government support documents and contractual hosting agreements, demonstrating the commitment of the relevant authorities and stakeholders.
"However, certain government guarantees, particularly those relating to safety and security and tax, contain certain qualifications which have been duly noted in the legal evaluation.
"While certain contractual matters remain subject to further discussion, the bidder's proactive engagement with FIFA and the substantial lead-in time provide a sound basis for resolving these outstanding issues."
English FA chair Debbie Hewitt addressed the congress after the bid's success had been confirmed.
"Thank you for your trust and confidence in awarding us the FIFA Women's World Cup 2035," Hewitt said.
"We're deeply honoured by your support and grateful for the opportunity to host the pinnacle of women's football on behalf of the global football family.
"As we said throughout our bid, we want this to be your FIFA Women's World Cup, a World Cup for everyone.
"Together, we will celebrate the power of women's football, inspire the next generation, and unite fans from every corner of the world. We look forward to welcoming you to the United Kingdom in 2035 and just as importantly, to working closely with you all in the years ahead to deliver an exceptional FIFA Women's World Cup that the entire football community can be proud of."
- 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup: Format, who has qualified ahead of playoffs?
- England World Cup playoff squad: Isobel Goodwin and Katie Cox named
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: "The world is coming to the United Kingdom. In 2035 the biggest tournament in women's sport will be played in cities across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, bringing visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country.
"Our players have inspired a generation of girls. In 2035 that generation will watch the best in the world play on their doorstep -- and some of them will be on the pitch. But the impact of this World Cup will go much further. It will reach into communities across the country, bring more people into the game and leave a legacy that lasts long after the final whistle."

items.title: Houston says Herrera available for Dynamo playoff opener amid MLS probe
items.summary:
MLS is gathering information regarding the reported arrest of Houston Dynamo FC midfielder Héctor Herrera for suspicion of driving while intoxicated ahead of the team's first game of the best-of-three round one series against the San Jose Earthquakes on Nov. 24.
"Major League Soccer is aware of an i
items.text:
MLS is gathering information regarding the reported arrest of Houston Dynamo FC midfielder Héctor Herrera for suspicion of driving while intoxicated ahead of the team's first game of the best-of-three round one series against the San Jose Earthquakes on Nov. 24.
"Major League Soccer is aware of an incident involving Houston Dynamo midfielder Héctor Herrera," MLS said in a statement to ESPN. "The League is gathering additional information and will refrain from further comment pending a review of the matter."
Houston Dynamo head coach Ben Olsen confirmed that as of Monday, Nov. 23, Herrera is eligible to feature in the playoff match against the Earthquakes.
Multiple reports said Herrera was charged with suspicion of DWI in Montgomery County, Texas, on Saturday. The Dynamo told ESPN on Sunday the club was aware of an incident involving Herrera.
"It's all in the league's hands. So far, he's available to play tomorrow," Olsen said in a press conference Monday.
Olsen added that Herrera's situation is not ideal, but does not present a distraction for the rest of the team ahead of the playoff match.
"The incident in question is Friday night, all right? And don't want to get into too many details. Is it ideal? No, but by and large, it's not a huge distraction. It's not ideal. But, you know, the group is a very healthy one, and we all have love for Hector, and when these things creep up, you deal with them in the right way, through process," Olsen added.
"It's been addressed, and it's been put to bed. The team is in a good place. This is not any excuse. Throughout the season, things like this happened, you know? And you, whether it's family members or, you know, things happen throughout seasons, and you address them, and you move on.
"And this isn't, again, the first thing that's happened this year, that we've had to address as a group, and all our focus right now is on trying to advance against a really good team, and I really don't even want to get into any more questions on Hector, frankly, because I think right now, the focus should be on our group, and the opportunity in front of us against San Jose."
Herrera previously faced MLS sanctions when he was sent off in 2024 for spitting on a referee. The Houston Dynamo chose to deny his 2025 contract extension following the incident, prior to re-signing Herrera in 2026.
The midfielder briefly featured for Liga MX side Toluca in 2025, before returning to MLS.
Herrera has recorded nine goals and 25 assists in 99 MLS regular season and playoff appearances for the Dynamo across four seasons. He played in 30 regular season games in 2026 since rejoining the club.
ESPN writer Cesar Hernandez contributed to this report.

items.title: Son Heung-Min: Thomas Müller spot-on about lack of pressure in MLS
items.summary:
LAFC forward Son Heung-Min has backed Thomas Müller's comments about the "careless" playing style in the MLS and the lack of pressure that players feel due to the absence of a promotion/relegation system.
Last week, Vancouver Whitecaps star Müller said it is difficult to compare the MLS to the Premi
items.text:
LAFC forward Son Heung-Min has backed Thomas Müller's comments about the "careless" playing style in the MLS and the lack of pressure that players feel due to the absence of a promotion/relegation system.
Last week, Vancouver Whitecaps star Müller said it is difficult to compare the MLS to the Premier League or other European leagues because "there is no relegation. There is no big pressure."
Son, who moved to the MLS in 2025 after a lengthy spell at Tottenham Hotspur, said Müller was "spot on" when asked about the German's remarks by reporters.
"The MLS is getting big, big name players are coming to the MLS but sometimes you feel there's less pressure because there isn't relegation.
"I can't control that but I'm enjoying this league...But I think Thomas was spot on. I thoroughly agree. He had an amazing career in the Bundesliga and he feels he's right to say it," the South Korea star said.
"I was in the Premier League -- every week, it's the biggest pressure. If you're not performing, if you're not playing well, if your team starts struggling or is in the bottom half of the table then you're having a difficult time.
"I think it makes it more fun. I want the best for the MLS, so maybe they can look into it and do something."
Müller, the most decorated German player of all time, sparked a conversation around the MLS' system of no promotion or relegation with his comments.
"[In Europe with relegation] The players have maybe no contracts for next year when you go down, so the playing style changes," the former Bayern Munich man said at the time. "When you play a bottom of the league team in Europe they fight for their lives. And sometimes I have the feeling, because of the [MLS] system, the playing style is a little bit more, let's say, optimistic, or careless, defensively.
- Philadelphia's Cavan Sullivan wins MLS Young Player of the Year award
- How B.J. Callaghan's long, winding coaching journey led to Nashville success
- Reports: Dynamo's Herrera charged with DWI, club aware of 'incident'
"So a little bit, just a little bit more, the French would say, laissez faire," he said. "That's maybe good for seeing some nice offensive plays when the games are opening up. When I compare it I see sometimes really, really good individual actions in players.
"What I miss sometimes is maybe the consistency, the good and the bad, the gap is bigger.
"[In MLS] There is, oh yeah, we do a rebuild," he said. "Nobody is happy to lose but it's totally different when you fight for getting relegated. Maybe yeah, you lose budget for the next year, the whole club. You lose people working at the club when the budget changes. It's totally different for fans."

items.title: Spirit fire González after losing NWSL Championship for 3rd straight season
items.summary:
The Washington Spirit have fired head coach Adrián González following the team's loss in Saturday's NWSL Championship, the team confirmed on Monday.
Washington's loss on Saturday marked the third straight season in which the team was defeated in the NWSL Championship.
González was the head coach of
items.text:
The Washington Spirit have fired head coach Adrián González following the team's loss in Saturday's NWSL Championship, the team confirmed on Monday.
Washington's loss on Saturday marked the third straight season in which the team was defeated in the NWSL Championship.
González was the head coach of the Spirit in the past two finals. He was an assistant to Jonathan Giráldez in 2024 after serving as acting head coach earlier that year.
"We are grateful to Adrián for his leadership and the success he has helped bring to the Spirit over the past three seasons," Spirit president of soccer operations Haley Carter said in a statement. "He has led the team with class and professionalism and made a lasting contribution to this club. As we plan for the Spirit's future, all parties believe a change in leadership is necessary to build on that success and achieve our long-term sporting goals."
Players were informed of the news on Monday after González was fired on Sunday, sources told ESPN.
Washington lost 2-1 to the Kansas City Current at Audi Field on Saturday in the NWSL Championship.
A source with knowledge of the Spirit's thinking said Saturday's loss was not the driving force in the team's decision, and that the Spirit felt a change was needed to move the team forward.
Washington's announcement on Monday stated that the team and González had "mutually agreed to part ways," and it included a statement from González.
"I'm incredibly proud of what we've accomplished together at the Washington Spirit and grateful to the players, staff, ownership and supporters for their commitment and support throughout my time here," González said in a statement. "It has been an honor to lead this group, and I'm especially proud of the resilience and character the team has shown."
González joined the Spirit in early 2024 to serve as interim coach ahead of the arrival of Jonatan Giráldez, who left FC Barcelona to become the Spirit's head coach that year.
Washington finished second in the 2024 regular season and runners-up in the playoffs, losing to the Orlando Pride in the 2024 NWSL Championship.
Giráldez left the Spirit midway through the 2025 season to become head coach of OL Lyonnes, which has the same owner, Michelle Kang. González then became head coach of the team and guided the Spirit to another second-place finish in 2025 before losing to Gotham FC in the NWSL Championship.
This year was González's only full year as head coach. Washington finished the regular season in third place before losing Saturday's NWSL Championship on home soil against Kansas City.
Carter joined the Spirit late last year after serving as the architect of Orlando's run to the 2024 NWSL Shield and NWSL Championship.
The team said that "a comprehensive search" is underway for its next head coach.

items.title: Sources: Man Utd to appeal Yoro red card against Liverpool
items.summary:
Manchester United have notified the Football Association of their intention to appeal Leny Yoro's red card in the 4-0 defeat to Liverpool, sources have told ESPN.
Yoro was dismissed in the eighth minute at Anfield on Sunday after a challenge on Alexander Isak.
The Frenchman was deemed to have denied
items.text:
Manchester United have notified the Football Association of their intention to appeal Leny Yoro's red card in the 4-0 defeat to Liverpool, sources have told ESPN.
Yoro was dismissed in the eighth minute at Anfield on Sunday after a challenge on Alexander Isak.
The Frenchman was deemed to have denied a clear goal-scoring opportunity by referee Michael Oliver, a view backed up by VAR.
United head coach Mauricio Pochettino questioned the decision in his post-match news conference. He also compared the incident to a similar situation involving Bryan Mbeumo in the Liverpool penalty area which was not deemed to be a foul.
Sources have told ESPN that United's view is that Isak's heavy touch meant Senne Lammens would have gathered the ball before the striker had the chance to shoot.
Club bosses have informed the FA they will appeal the red card.
United conceded immediately after Yoro was sent off with Dominik Szoboszlai scoring from the resulting free-kick.
- Man United need big January transfer spend to avoid Premier League relegation
- Mauricio Pochettino gets reality check as Liverpool ruin his Man United debut
- Bruno Fernandes disputes Leny Yoro red card in Liverpool's rout of Man United
Liverpool went on to win 4-0 to hand Pochettino a heavy defeat in his first game since taking over from Michael Carrick.
The result leaves United 19th in the table and mired in relegation trouble after 11 games of the season.
What did Pochettino, Fernandes say about Yoro's red card?
Pochettino's perspective on the Yoro incident was: "I wasn't agreeing with the red card because I think the situation was when Isak control the ball, the ball wasn't in his control. The centre-back [Yoro] was running with him, Isak saw the control wasn't good and it is normal you delay, you stop to run, in that moment Yoro came from the back, and it is like a touch like this and you go down."
United midfielder Bruno Fernandes told BBC Sport: "I can understand the fall, but it's never a red card.
"I think it's too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR, seated, with such a long time to see and put it back, go forward, put it back, do it in slow motion, whatsoever.
"To make a mistake like this can change a game. But obviously, then, it's not because of them that we concede the goal from the free-kick, but it changes completely the flow of the game."
Kobbie Mainoo's verdict was: "I feel like the game was killed early with a decision by the referee that I don't think can be a red card.
"The ball is already with the keeper when he's gone down, two players running at full speed. I mean, it's impossible to be a red, but it is what it is.
Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola disagreed, saying: "I think it's a situation where [Yoro] is clearly the last man, it is clearly a foul. Would Alex or the 'keeper arrive first to the ball? We will never know. It's a clear foul, he's a last player, Alex goes against the 'keeper."

Philadelphia Union midfielder Cavan Sullivan has been selected as the MLS Young Player of the Year for his breakthrough performance as a 17-year-old.
The award honors the top player who was born Jan. 1, 2004 or later. Sullivan is the youngest player ever to win the award.
Red Bull New York had the r
items.text:
Philadelphia Union midfielder Cavan Sullivan has been selected as the MLS Young Player of the Year for his breakthrough performance as a 17-year-old.
The award honors the top player who was born Jan. 1, 2004 or later. Sullivan is the youngest player ever to win the award.
Red Bull New York had the runner-up and third-place finishers in the voting. Julian Hall finished second and Adri Mehmeti was third.
Sullivan had nine goals and 14 assists over 28 games in his first MLS season as a full-time player. He had either a goal or an assist in 10 straight matches, the longest such streak by a teenager in MLS history.
Sullivan was called up to the United States men's national team in September and became the second-youngest player in U.S. history to start a match.
MLS players vote on this award along with club technical staff and media.

items.title: NWSL Goalkeeper of the Year Berger leaves Gotham FC to join Union Berlin
items.summary:
Ann-Katrin Berger, the National Women's Soccer League's Goalkeeper of the Year this season, has joined German club Union Berlin as a free agent after three seasons with Gotham FC.
Gotham acquired the Germany national team keeper from Chelsea in 2024 for an undisclosed transfer fee. She started in al
items.text:
Ann-Katrin Berger, the National Women's Soccer League's Goalkeeper of the Year this season, has joined German club Union Berlin as a free agent after three seasons with Gotham FC.
Gotham acquired the Germany national team keeper from Chelsea in 2024 for an undisclosed transfer fee. She started in all 73 regular-season matches she played with Gotham, with 29 shutouts.
During her time with the team, Gotham won the 2025 NWSL Championship, the 2026 NWSL Shield for best record and the 2024-25 CONCACAF Champions Cup.
"Ann has been instrumental in the success we've achieved over the past three seasons, and her impact on this club extends well beyond her performances in goal," Yael Averbuch West, Gotham's president of soccer operations, said in a statement. "Her consistency and ability to deliver in the biggest moments helped shape a championship-winning team."
Berger had 11 shutouts this season, making her the NWSL's first goalkeeper with at least 10 clean sheets in back-to-back seasons. She also won the league's goalkeeper of the year in the 2024 season.
Berger was goalkeeper for the German team that won the bronze medal at the Paris Olympics. She was also in goal when Germany reached the semifinals of the 2025 European Championship.
Berger, 36, will join Union Berlin in January, the Bundesliga club said.
"Union have courted me intensively and over a long period of time, which I really appreciate," Berger said in a statement released by Union Berlin.
"The path the club has taken in recent years is remarkable. I would like to use my experience to help drive this ambitious team forward. After so many years abroad, I'm really looking forward to returning to the Bundesliga. My thanks go to Gotham FC for a wonderful and successful time."

items.text:
US adds Megaspeed, firm at centre of Nvidia scandal, to export control list
Bureau of Security and Industry adds Singapore-based firm and six other entities to export control list.
The United States government has added the Singapore-based company at the centre of the spying claims surrounding Nvidia to its trade blacklist.
The Bureau of Security and Industry (BIS) placed Megaspeed International and six other firms on entity list on Monday, hours after Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia as CEO in a stunning comeback that sent tech stocks soaring.
Megaspeed and the six other entities were determined to be “acting contrary to the national security or foreign policy interests of the United States,” BIS said in a filing to the Federal Register.
The designations mean that any company or person seeking to ship advanced US technology, such as Nvidia top-end graphics processing units (GPUs) used to power AI, to the firms first must obtain an export licence.
The other six entities added to the list are MSFusion, PT Megaspeed International, and Speedmatrix, based in Malaysia; Apex Enterprise Solutions and Swiftdata, based in Singapore; and Megaspeed, based in Thailand.
More to follow…

items.title: What could Democrats do with their expanding congressional majority?
items.summary:
What could Democrats do with their expanding congressional majority?
The Democratic Party is debating how best to use its large margin of victory in the US midterm elections.
The Democratic Party has continued to expand its already sizeable majorities in the United States Congress as counting conclu
items.text:
What could Democrats do with their expanding congressional majority?
The Democratic Party is debating how best to use its large margin of victory in the US midterm elections.
The Democratic Party has continued to expand its already sizeable majorities in the United States Congress as counting concludes in the final races of the 2026 midterm elections.
As of Monday, the Democrats hold a 258-seat majority in the 435-member House of Representatives. Four races remain uncalled.
All the races have been decided, meanwhile, for the Senate, where Democrats gained a 56-seat majority out of 100 total seats.
Flipping both chambers gives the party a strong hand to shape legislation during the last two years of Trump’s term in office.
How might the Democrats approach their role in government once the new Congress is sworn in on January 3? Find out in this quick explainer.
What do the results say?
The midterm results give Democrats their largest House majority since 1992 and their largest Senate majority in more than a decade. Republicans, meanwhile, saw their tally in the House drop to 173 seats, their lowest figure in years.
The vote also served as a firm rebuke of Trump’s second term as president, with voters venting their frustration over cost-of-living issues, the US-Israel war on Iran, aggressive immigration raids and corruption.
Democratic victories also extended well beyond traditional left-wing strongholds, with candidates racking up wins in Republican-led states such as Texas, Mississippi and South Carolina.
Which races remain?
Four House seats have yet to be called: one in Minnesota, one in Tennessee, and two in Louisiana that will be settled by a run-off on December 12.
Those races could see the Democrats further expand their majority in the House. The final count is now a question of just how large the party’s majority will be.
What will Democrats do with their majority?
Democrats have long pledged to use any congressional majorities they win as a check on Trump’s agenda.
But the scale of their success in the 2026 midterms has prompted discussion about embracing a more ambitious legislative agenda.
In the House of Representatives, Democrats have outlined a 100-day agenda that includes potentially reversing tax cuts that largely benefit wealthy earners and restoring healthcare subsidies that expired under Trump.
Lawmakers have also said that they will act to end the war on Iran, although divisions remain within the party over how to rein in Trump’s military actions. Under the US Constitution, Congress alone can authorise military operations.
Progressives have accused the party’s moderate wing of playing down expectations of firm steps to end the war, including cutting off funding.
Democrats have also pledged to use their newfound position to exercise oversight over the executive branch by launching probes and issuing subpoenas.
On Monday, for example, House Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries said that a Democrat-led Congress would conduct a “swift, thorough, and wide-ranging” investigation into the actions of the chip manufacturer Nvidia.
He also said it would delve into the “corrupt abuse of power” by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.
In the Senate, Democrats have also threatened to block Trump’s nominees for high-level government positions, which require the chamber’s confirmation.
What role will Trump play?
While Democrats will hold substantial majorities in both chambers of Congress, Trump will retain the power to veto legislation.
Some lawmakers, however, have tried to persuade the president that he could benefit from working with Democrats after his party’s stark defeat in the midterms.
Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed, for example, has shared a series of tongue-in-cheek social media posts suggesting that a universal healthcare programme — a long-term progressive goal — could be named after the president in a bid to win his support.
“Donald, this is on the table,” El-Sayed said in a social media post showing a card for a hypothetical health insurance programme titled “Trumpcare”. “Guarantee healthcare for every American, from cradle to grave.”
Could Trump work with the Democrats?
There is little evidence, however, to suggest that Trump is planning a political pivot after the midterms.
Within a week of the vote, for instance, Trump named Stephen Miller — one of the architects of his hardline policies on immigration — as White House chief of staff.
The staffing shake-up was seen as a doubling-down on right-wing policy priorities.
While Trump has, at times, suggested that he could cooperate with Democratic lawmakers, he has also promised to use his veto power aggressively.
He has also taken to social media to disparage Chuck Schumer, who is currently seeking to become the next Senate majority leader, a position he previously held from 2021 to 2025.
“It is going to be very hard for me to work with Chuck Schumer should he become Senate Majority Leader,” Trump said in a Truth Social post on Sunday.
“He failed badly as ‘Leader’ once before, one of the worst in history, and I have little doubt that he will fail again.”
Trump’s White House has also threatened to take action if Democrats aggressively use their oversight powers in Congress.
“Members of the new Congress have evinced a clear intent to transgress” the constitutional limits of their power, White House counsel Will Scharf wrote in a letter on November 9, gesturing to the prospect of congressional investigations.

items.text:
Zelensky urges four-way peace talks with Russia, Europe and US 'as soon as possible'
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is calling for a new round of negotiations involving Ukraine, Russia, the United States and European leaders, saying Kyiv is ready to meet as early as Tuesday.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday called for new negotiations with Russia involving European leaders to be held as soon as possible and repeated a plea for his country to join the NATO alliance.
Zelensky, speaking by video to a gathering of lawmakers from NATO countries in Berlin, welcomed the latest push for peace talks with Moscow.
"We must do everything to make sure that the four-party meeting -- Ukraine, Europe, America and Russia -- happens as soon as possible. We are ready to do this. Literally tomorrow," Zelensky said.
"We have heard from our partners that they want to try to make it happen before Christmas. We hope it happens sooner."
European governments have been excluded from past discussions and their push to join talks has gained prominence in recent weeks.
Zelensky, whose country has been battling a full-scale Russian invasion since February 2022, has repeatedly called for a path to full membership in NATO -- and not simply receiving security guarantees from alliance countries.
He argued that Ukraine's combat experience, innovative defence industry and large military would all benefit other allies.
"NATO is the answer -- and with a strong Ukrainian army, NATO itself is guaranteed to be stronger," Zelensky told the Berlin gathering.
A number of NATO leaders have expressed hesitation about bringing Ukraine into the alliance.
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, speaking after Zelensky at the same event on Monday, underscored the alliance's support for Ukraine but noted that joining would require unanimous support.
"Not all NATO allies agree at this moment (on) letting Ukraine become a member," Rutte said, though he also firmly rejected the idea that outside powers like Russia could dictate who joins the alliance.
During a gathering of Ukrainian supporters in Berlin last week, US envoy Jared Kushner said that Washington might consider offering Ukraine a security guarantee similar to that provided under Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty as part of a peace settlement.
But in his remarks on Monday, Zelensky said major questions remain about how such guarantees would work without a full NATO commitment.
"Which countries will support Ukraine if Ukraine is attacked again? What exactly will our partners do in response? Which troops will be stationed on our territory in advance? How much will all this cost? And will it really work?
"All of this is not easy and so far we have not heard clear specific answers," Zelensky said.
The Ukrainian leader also repeated a call for NATO countries to provide more air defence weapons, urging them to empty their stockpiles to allow Ukraine to repel Russian airstrikes.
"Missiles that can stop Russian ballistic missiles should not be sitting in warehouses collecting dust," he said.
(FRANCE 24 with AFP)

items.text:
King Charles and Elton John pay tribute to Australian music legend Molly Meldrum
- Published
King Charles and Elton John have paid tribute to Australian music industry legend Molly Meldrum, who died aged 83 after a long illness.
Meldrum's family said he "passed away peacefully" at a hospital in Melbourne in the early hours of Monday morning.
The music promoter and broadcaster, born Ian Alexander Meldrum, helped define the nation's music tastes for decades, championing local artists like INXS and Kylie Minogue and global acts like Abba.
Known for his chaotic demeanour and trademark Stetson hat, he interviewed an array of stars, with the king on Monday calling him "a true giant of the music industry".
Born in Victoria in 1943, Meldrum displayed a love of music from an early age and went on to host the Australian Broadcasting Corporation's music television programme Countdown, and later a segment on variety show Hey Hey, It's Saturday.
Meldrum in 2014 became the first person who was not a recording artist to be inducted into the Australian Recording Industry Association (Aria) Hall of Fame.
Meldrum lived with an acquired brain injury after falling from a ladder in 2011.
"Affectionately dubbed 'the Guru', Molly was the heartbeat, the champion and the spirit of Australian music," a statement from Meldrum's family said.
Among his most famous interviews was a 1977 sit-down with King Charles, in which Meldrum could not calm his jitters.
He stumbled over his lines, declaring: "Your Royal Highness... Oh, oh, I'm sweating like a pig".
King Charles reflected on the infamous interview for Countdown's 40th anniversary special, saying: "There is an old showbusiness saying which warns never to work with animals or children. But nobody prepared me for Molly Meldrum".
On Monday, an aide to the King said he had been "deeply saddened" to hear of Meldrum's death.
"His Majesty's interview with Molly is a moment he and many others will never forget - he hopes that interview will once again raise a few smiles as Australians honour Molly's legacy as a true giant of the music industry."
Elton John - a friend and regular interviewee - paid tribute to him as "an Australian legend and an institution", while pop star Kylie Minogue said she would be turning up the music in his honour.
"As a kid, I watched Molly Meldrum on Countdown every single weekend, in awe of the show and the magic it brought to our little TV in the lounge room."
"He championed so many Aussie artists and welcomed international artists to Australia in his own wonderful and inimitable way. I'm so grateful for his unwavering love and support."
Australia's Arts Minister Tony Burke said the country had lost an icon: "One of his greatest legacies will be the generations of Australians who grew up with his unmistakable enthusiasm and love of music."

items.text:
Trump calls to ‘expedite’ US federal executions, blasts Gavin Newsom
The US president used his podium to attack the California governor for a decision to commute 548 death sentences.
United States President Donald Trump has reaffirmed his support for the death penalty in an event that doubled as a platform to attack one of his most visible critics, California Governor Gavin Newsom.
On Monday, Trump spoke at the Department of Justice in Washington, DC, where he was joined by the families of crime victims and his attorney general, Todd Blanche.
“The ultimate crimes deserve the ultimate punishment,” Trump said of the death penalty, calling it a cornerstone of “ virtually every society throughout history, at least every successful society”.
“Under the Trump administration, we are bringing it back, and we will not stop in our pursuit of justice. We will not yield.”
He concluded the appearance by signing a presidential directive ordering the Department of Justice to seek the death penalty in murder cases involving children, rape and human trafficking.
The directive also pushes for the attorney general to “expedite” executions for those on federal death row.
As part of his speech, Trump called on Congress to pass the Just Punishment for Murder Act, a bill sponsored by Republican Representative Brandon Gill, which the president said would “strengthen the death penalty in America”.
But he dedicated much of his remarks to slamming Newsom, a Democrat widely seen as a possible contender for the 2028 presidential race.
Newsom’s second term as governor will end on January 4. Under California term limits, he was ineligible to run again in the 2026 midterm elections.
Still, the governor and former San Francisco mayor has carved a national profile for himself as a proxy for Democrats during high-stakes political campaigns — and as a critic of Trump.
Trump, however, zeroed in on one of Newsom’s final major actions while in office: commuting the sentences of those on California’s death row.
On November 5, two days after the midterms, Newsom announced that the 548 people sentenced to death in California would instead be sentenced to life without the possibility of parole.
He described the action as an extension of the moratorium on executions he put in place after taking office in 2019.
“I could not remain true to my values and oversee the killing of people with death warrants in California,” he wrote in an open letter.
He nevertheless denounced the harm the 548 people had caused.
“Many Californians feel that those who commit brutal crimes deserve to die,” Newsom wrote. “But as Governor, I have concluded the state cannot morally kill them.”
He called on Californians to let the 548 people “die in obscurity” while remembering their victims.
Trump, however, framed the mass commutation as an effort to help “evil monsters” escape justice.
“This afternoon, we come together to stand against the travesty and to wrap our arms around the families of victims who were so cruelly betrayed by bad government and our political system,” Trump said.
The president proceeded to launch barbs at Newsom, calling him “ a terrible governor” who “ stole away the only closure” the victims’ families “might ever have”.
He then invited several family members on stage to denounce Newsom’s decision.
“ You took the only justice we had and left families feeling abandoned by the state that promised to protect us,” Sandra Friend, the mother of eight-year-old murder victim Michael Lyons, said in her remarks, directed at Newsom.
In anticipation of Monday’s news conference, Newsom also released statements from families that supported his choice.
“When victims are this divided, the death penalty shouldn’t be the answer. Victims deserve so much more than a promise of justice through vengeance,” Jess Nichol, the sister of murder victim Polly Klaas, said in one of the statements.
“They deserve counselling, medical care, financial support, and a justice system that helps them heal. I want something better for survivors: real, tangible support.”
The tit-for-tat between Newsom and Trump comes as support for the death penalty has slumped in recent years.
A November poll released by the research firm Gallup found that 49 percent of US adults support the death penalty, the lowest rate since 1971.
Opponents of the death penalty have frequently pointed to the prevalence of botched executions and the possibility that innocent people may be executed.
The Death Penalty Information Center, a nonprofit, has found that approximately 202 people formerly on death row were later found to be wrongfully convicted. The exoneration rate, it said, was one for every eight people executed in the US.
Death penalty cases also typically tend to result in longer court battles and higher costs.
Before Newsom’s mass commutation, California reportedly had the largest death row in the Western Hemisphere, representing roughly a quarter of the country’s death sentences.
Newsom’s successor, Governor-elect Xavier Becerra, has pledged to continue the death penalty moratorium once sworn in.
But that policy puts California at odds with a push under Trump to embrace the death penalty and expand execution methods.
Upon taking office for a second term on January 20, 2025, Trump signed the first of several executive orders aimed at “restoring the death penalty”.
He pushed to have execution be the de facto punishment for the murder of law enforcement officers, as well as for murder cases where undocumented immigrants are the defendants.
In April, the Trump administration also said it would prioritise the use of the death penalty by expanding the acceptable methods for federal execution, including firing squads.
In October, Trump’s Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced that one execution by firing squad — that of the Fort Hood shooter, Nidal Hasan — would be livestreamed to the public, prompting backlash.
Trump later walked back the announcement, amid reports that he did not realise Hassan

items.text:
Borno school enrolment nearly doubles after years of conflict
Despite rising enrolment, violence, displacement and poverty keep children out of school in northeastern state.
Maiduguri, Nigeria – During years of Boko Haram violence, Maryam Umar’s school in Baga, a town in northeastern Nigeria’s Borno State, was forced to close as violence displaced families and disrupted education across the region.
The closure of the Higher Islamic College in Baga in the Kukawa Local Government Area was part of a wider crisis that deprived thousands of children of regular schooling.
With educational activities now resuming, Umar, a teacher, welcomed efforts to reopen schools and provide learning materials, telling Al Jazeera that the interventions were helping restore education in communities devastated by years of conflict.
Across Borno, authorities said school enrolment has risen sharply as damaged classrooms are repaired and families are encouraged to send their children back to school.
Enrolment in public and private schools reached 1,418,279 learners in 2025, up from 766,551 during the 2017-2018 academic session, according to the state government.
Yet officials estimated that almost 800,000 children remain out of school, highlighting the challenges facing a state where more than a decade of conflict has displaced communities and devastated public services.
The figures suggest progress in expanding access but reveal little about regular attendance, teaching quality or whether children who have missed years of education are catching up.
Rebuilding after years of violence
Borno has been at the centre of Boko Haram violence since the armed group launched its campaign in northeastern Nigeria in 2009.
Schools were among the institutions affected as attacks, displacement and a prolonged lack of security forced families to abandon their homes. In some communities, education became impossible as classrooms closed and teachers and pupils fled.
The state government has made school reconstruction a priority, building new facilities and rehabilitating classrooms damaged by conflict and flooding.
“In response, our administration has constructed 104 new schools and rehabilitated 2,931 classrooms and related facilities,” Governor Babagana Umara Zulum said during the commissioning of educational projects in Maiduguri in March.
According to the governor, the estimated number of out-of-school children has fallen from about 2.2 million at the height of the crisis to fewer than 800,000.
Borno Commissioner for Education, Science, Technology and Innovation Lawan Abba Wakilbe said the increase in enrolment reflects renewed confidence among parents.
But increased enrolment does not necessarily mean children are attending regularly or receiving the support they need after years of disrupted learning.
The available figures also provide little indication of whether the supply of qualified teachers and learning materials has kept pace with the growing number of pupils.
A generation returning to classrooms
For 12-year-old Fatima Mahmud Umar, a student at the Junior Secondary School One in Maiduguri, education offers an opportunity to pursue ambitions that years of violence have threatened for children across Borno.
Wearing a blue and white chequered hijab and her school uniform, Fatima spoke to Al Jazeera about her hopes for the future.
She expressed gratitude to her parents for supporting her education and said she hopes to become a good ambassador for her community.
Fatima also welcomed government investment in schools, including efforts to support both Islamic and Western education.
But many children across Borno have yet to regain access to regular schooling.
Violence, displacement and poverty continue to create obstacles, particularly for families struggling to rebuild their lives after years of upheaval.
Even where schools have reopened, children who missed months or years of lessons may struggle to catch up with their peers while teachers must accommodate pupils with widely different levels of preparation.
For returning students, enrolment is only the first step. Their prospects also depend on whether schools can provide the support needed to help them progress.
Rural communities left behind
The challenge is particularly pressing in rural communities, where distance, violence and limited resources can make regular schooling difficult.
In the Gubio Local Government Area, residents have raised concerns about children who remain outside formal education despite the government’s reconstruction efforts.
Bukar Abdullahi, 49, highlighted the need to enrol more children during a town hall meeting in Gubio.
While commending the state government for investing in education, Abdullahi drew attention to the difficulties facing rural communities.
For families living far from functioning schools, distance can remain an obstacle. Financial pressures and concerns about safety may also affect decisions about whether children attend.
Although the government’s figures suggest improved access, they do not show how evenly progress is distributed between urban centres and rural communities.
Addressing those disparities will require more than classrooms. Schools also need qualified teachers, learning materials and measures to help families keep their children enrolled.
Expanding Islamic education
Alongside conventional schools, Borno authorities are seeking to widen educational opportunities through Arabic and Islamic institutions.
Through the Borno State Arabic and Sangaya Education Board, the government is working to integrate aspects of traditional Islamic learning into a system offering recognised qualifications and pathways to further study.
The establishment of Higher Islamic Colleges is part of that effort.
“This intervention reflects our commitment to building an inclusive education system that integrates spiritual development with academic and vocational advancement,” Zulum said.

items.text:
Dad who discovered daughter's murder on Facebook feels ignored by South African police
- Published
Tuku Nkosiyaphantsi found out his daughter had been killed from a post on Facebook.
It was August and he hadn't been able to reach 27-year-old Okuhle for days, although it wasn't unusual for her to drop out of contact from time to time.
Then one Saturday, two of Tuku's neighbours called him to say that they had seen that Okuhle had been reported missing by police on Facebook. They had also seen a photo of what appeared to be Okuhle injured.
"When I looked at this photo, I saw that the person in it was dead, and when I looked closer I realised it was Okuhle," says Tuku, 50.
After seeing the image, Tuku phoned a police officer he knew. The policeman confirmed the woman in the picture had been killed and her body dumped near a river in Kokstad, an agricultural hub in South Africa's KwaZulu-Natal province, in the east of the country.
But because the morgue was closed for the weekend, it wasn't until Monday morning that Tuku was able to identify Okuhle's body.
When he did, Tuku saw she had been mutilated and her face badly beaten.
"It was very painful, so much that I cannot accept it."
Okuhle had two children, aged nine and three, and was a civil engineering student.
She is among 581 women who were killed in the country between July and September, according to the South African Police Service.
Overall, there were 5,590 murders - 204 fewer than in the same period last year.
It is the first time police have broken down murders by gender, so it is unclear whether the number of women killed is an increase or decrease on previous years.
There has been a renewed national outcry this year about the scale of violence against women after the partially naked and bruised bodies of 12 women were found dumped in public areas in Ekurhuleni, a district to the east of Johannesburg, this summer.
South Africa has one of the highest rates of gender-based violence and femicide - the intentional killing of a woman or girl - in the world.
Am I Next? Fear and Survival in South Africa
The BBC World Service visits communities struggling to confront widespread violence against women
In response to this summer's killings, President Cyril Ramaphosa promised safety audits across every municipality to identify and address dangerous spaces for women, as well as an increased police presence in the worst-affected areas.
But in places like Kokstad and Kempton Park, both in Ekurhuleni, the BBC World Service saw people taking the protection of women into their own hands.
For Tuku, that means investigating his daughter's killing himself.
Months after she was killed, he says no-one has been arrested.
"It was just silent after we buried Okuhle - there was nothing at all. I so wish the police would stand up and investigate."
He believes police failed to review CCTV footage from a local government building in the town that may have shown who his daughter was with on the day she disappeared. The footage is wiped every seven days, he says.
The BBC approached the South African Police Service for comment but at the time of publication, no response had been received.
The police service has previously acknowledged shortcomings in its overall response to gender-based violence and femicide, adding that it was continuing to invest in addressing these challenges. Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia has said there needs to be "greater efforts" to prevent violence against women and children.
According to a 2024 report by the South African Medical Research Council, the number of unsolved cases of femicide was growing.
This year, Amnesty International said South Africa's police service was "under-resourced, poorly equipped, and insufficiently trained to respond effectively and sensitively to gender-based violence".
Tuku says he is now searching for CCTV footage and seeking out people who knew his daughter in the hope of finding leads.
Despite Ramaphosa's promises, he has little faith anything will change.
"I listened to Ramaphosa. The government acts only when something happened. We in Kokstad, we feel like we are ignored and unseen. The government does not care for us."
Asked earlier this month by the BBC what progress South Africa had made to keep women safe, Ramaphosa said the government would be allocating extra money in February's budget to deal with gender-based violence.
Speaking as he cast his vote in local elections, Ramaphosa added that the government had increased police numbers in the last three years "and we will continue to do so, so that there can be more visible policing".
Okuhle is not the only woman to be killed this year in Kokstad.
Between January and October this year, the bodies of five women and three very young children were found in the town, with arrests only taking place in two of the cases.
In response, this summer, the community set up street patrols and a curfew for women and children.
Since June, children have been told to be indoors by sunset and women by 21:00.
Kamvalethu Cetywayo, 34, from a local neighbourhood watch group, leads a group of around 15 men who patrol crime hotspots in the town at night, including areas where bodies have been found or trouble has been reported to them.
The patrols tend to take place between Thursday and Sunday because this is when people drink alcohol most heavily, says Kamvalethu.
Most of the patrollers carry sticks, whips and torches, but Kamvalethu has a licensed gun. He says the group will call police when they need back-up.
Asked how he feels about restricting the freedoms of women and children, Kamvalethu says the curfew helps keep them safe, is voluntary, and a temporary measure until police arrest the killers.
"With the resolution we made with the community, we get to assist them with this, but if people are refusing there's nothing we can do."
Even so, not all victims are attacked at night or on the streets.
Kgothatso Mojela was kidnapped on her way to work in 2018 in Kempto

items.text:
Who has made Troy's Premier League team of the week?
- Published
After every round of Premier League matches this season, BBC football pundit Troy Deeney will give you his team and manager of the week.
Here are this week's choices. Do you agree? Give us your thoughts using the comments form at the bottom of this page.
Konstantinos Tzolakis (Hull City): If you watched the Brighton game and wondered how on earth Hull won it was because Konstantinos Tzolakis was in goal. An unbelievable performance with five or six top-class saves. Big moments, big personality, he has stepped up every time. He's been one of the players of the season - I know it's a bit too early to crown people but if it stopped now he has to be goalkeeper of the season.
James Hill (Bournemouth): He backed up getting into the England squad. Sometimes when people get called up they start to get above their stations but he didn't do that at all. He was in a really good state of form. A cheeky assist as well but defensively solid. He has been in my team a few times now - a centre-half who does his job without complaining.
Malick Thiaw (Newcastle): He divides opinion but he played really well and got his goal.
Keane Lewis-Potter (Brentford): Two goals against Everton and that was before the sending-off of James Tarkowski. Performed well again. Sneaky bargain buy of the century to be honest.
Noah Okafor (Leeds): Two goals again. Leeds battered Chelsea and made them look unbelievably average. Nobody has been talking about how sneaky good Leeds have been, some really big performances this season.
Jack Rudoni (Coventry): Two assists in a must-win game against Crystal Palace. He stepped up big, fair play to him.
Elliott Anderson (Manchester City): The only person who actually showed a pulse in this game. He got a goal and showed pace and showed he wanted to be there. He tried his best to win a game of football.
Luca Williams-Barnett (Tottenham): Young man, a with goal and an assist. He just gave Spurs a spark we haven't seen for probably six or seven years now. He gave them that spark instantly and fair play to De Zerbi for putting him in. All the money spent, who knew it would be a home-grown talent in their youth team who would step up and really get the Spurs fans excited.

items.title: Tarkowski's first Premier League red ruins Moyes' night - was it deserved?
items.summary:
Tarkowski's first Premier League red ruins Moyes' night - was it deserved?
- Published
It had been some run for Everton captain James Tarkowski.
Prior to Monday night, the defender had received 74 yellow cards in the Premier League but had never been sent off - a top-flight record.
But that run came
items.text:
Tarkowski's first Premier League red ruins Moyes' night - was it deserved?
- Published
It had been some run for Everton captain James Tarkowski.
Prior to Monday night, the defender had received 74 yellow cards in the Premier League but had never been sent off - a top-flight record.
But that run came to an end at Brentford as he was given his first red card in his 351st Premier League appearance, although the decision has attracted plenty of debate.
His dismissal crucially means he will miss Sunday's Merseyside derby and also ruined David Moyes' record-breaking night as he took charge of his 593rd game as Everton boss - more than anyone else in the club's history.
The 4-0 loss was also the heaviest defeat Everton have had since Moyes returned to the club at the start of last year.
Tarkowski's dismissal proved a big talking point during and after the match, with opinions split on whether he should have gone. Even Moyes wasn't sure.
He told BBC Match of the Day: "My thoughts at the time, I didn't think it was but when I've looked at it again I think his foot high. Is there enough force for it to be a red card? Not sure about that."
Why did Tarkowski get sent off?
So what exactly happened?
Just 15 minutes after Keane Lewis-Potter scored his second deflected strike of the evening, Everton skipper Tarkowski thundered into a challenge on Brentford's Yehor Yarmoliuk.
He won the ball but also followed through with the challenge forcefully. Initially, referee Craig Pawson deemed a foul and a yellow card was enough.
But, after an intervention from the video assistant referee (VAR) and studying the replay, Pawson changed the yellow for a red.
The Premier League match centre said on X: "After VAR review, the referee overturned the original decision of yellow card for Tarkowski for the challenge on Yarmoliuk and issued a red card for serious foul play.
"VAR: 'Point of contact is on the shin. He's got speed and intensity. Studs are high.'
"REF: 'After review, Everton No.6 commits a challenge that endangers his opponent's safety, making contact with the studs onto the shin. Cancelling the yellow card - and a red card.'"
'Game's gone' or '100% red'? Experts are split
Referees are asked to take into account several considerations for what counts as serious foul play including the speed of the challenge, its intensity, force and what degree of control there was.
But, as always, there was plenty of debate about whether it was the correct decision.
BBC Sport's football issues correspondent Dale Johnson, said: "Really not sure about this as a VAR red card.
"Yes, Tarkowski absolutely ticks the boxes for speed and intensity and leading high with studs showing.
"But the question marks are that Tarkowski made only small contact and didn't have a straight leg when he did so.
"Maybe his reputation played a part? Remember, he wrongly escaped a VAR red card against Liverpool for a challenge, which was along the same lines. He won the ball and then followed through into Alexis Mac Allister. Thought that was a far stronger challenge."
BBC Radio 5 Live's - and former Blackburn Rovers striker - Chris Sutton, said on X: "Come on that's not a red… the game's gone."
Former Arsenal striker Alan Smith agreed the decision was harsh. He told Sky Sports: "Ten years ago we wouldn't have looked at it once and now we still [frame] it on the follow-through. I just can't see it.
"Only Tarkowski knows if he wanted to leave it high or if it was natural. The follow-through was just natural momentum.
"There's a bit of anger in there from Tarkowski and it's a little high but only he knows if he wanted to leave a little more on Yarmoliuk there."
Opinion was far from unanimous though, with both pundits in the Sky Sports studio adamant it was a clear red.
Former Liverpool centre-back Jamie Carragher said: "It's a red card. Tarkowski has got previous for tackles like that. He is a 90s defender, he tackles like that.
"He follows through with such force, it is excessive. You want to give him the benefit of the doubt but it's a red card."
He added: "You could argue was it a big enough mistake for VAR to get involved but I think we are splitting hairs. He doesn't need to do this."
While ex-Totenham defender Toby Alderweireld added: "It's a red card, he knows what he is doing. 100%."
'Never a red' or a 'clear' sending off - what you thought
Josh, Sheffield: Never a red for Tarkowski and I'm a Liverpool fan. What's he meant to do? Stop momentum. It's a good tackle and the player runs into the natural follow through
Robin, Essex: Another game ruined by VAR! Not straight leg tackle you can surely see he turned his foot around. Poor!
Rob, Manchester: These sorts of VAR decisions are making me turn off football. Why pay all that money to watch arbitrary decisions impact the game?
Lee: It is a sad day when a good tackle gets a player sent off. You slow anything down and dissect it you can find wrongs. Yellow was a bit much and the red ridiculous, we need ex players in the VAR decisions too.
Max, Oldham: What a load of nonsense the red card is. Tarkowski can't stop his momentum. VAR has ruined another game, plus what is the ref doing? He had a chance to stick with the yellow card. Another case of an official who has never played the game.
Paul, St Asaph: Tarkowski has got away with that same foul a few times. Do think he's the type of player to leave one in on purpose.
Anon: Yes it's a red - Tarkowski knows what he's doing, it's frustration and wanting to leave a bit on the player.
Chris, Chelmsford: He does it all the time at the borderline but about time he got one.
Woody, London: Lack of refinement masked as passion, classic Tarkowski tackle there… glad to see him off.
George, Birmingham: Studs up in a tackle, he has to go. A clear red card for me.
