items.title: Stalwart is now a drop-in replacement for Microsoft Exchange
items.summary:
Stalwart is now a drop-in replacement for Microsoft Exchange
For more than twenty years, “the mail server” in most companies meant Microsoft Exchange, and “the mail client” meant Outlook. Today we are releasing Stalwart 1.2.0, and with it Stalwart becomes a drop-in replacement for Microsoft Exchange
items.text:
Stalwart is now a drop-in replacement for Microsoft Exchange
For more than twenty years, “the mail server” in most companies meant Microsoft Exchange, and “the mail client” meant Outlook. Today we are releasing Stalwart 1.2.0, and with it Stalwart becomes a drop-in replacement for Microsoft Exchange.
Stalwart now implements the protocols that Exchange clients speak: MAPI over HTTP, Exchange Web Services (EWS), Exchange ActiveSync and Autodiscover. Outlook, Apple Mail and the mail apps on phones and tablets connect to Stalwart as they would to an Exchange server, with mail, calendars, contacts, tasks and notes in one account. Users type their email address and password, Autodiscover does the rest, and they keep working in the client they already know.
Exchange support is part of the open source Community edition, under the AGPL.
Exchange on premises in 2026
Section titled “Exchange on premises in 2026”
Before going into what Stalwart now does, it is worth looking at where self-hosted Exchange stands today, because it explains why so many organisations are looking for a way out.
Microsoft has not announced the end of Exchange Server. On paper, on-premises Exchange still exists. In practice, every road Microsoft is building leads to Exchange Online:
- Exchange 2016 and 2019 are out of support. Both reached end of support on 14 October 2025. Microsoft sold a paid Extended Security Update programme for a while, and according to press reports of an Exchange team statement, it ended in October 2026 with no further extension. Servers still running those versions receive no fixes of any kind.
- No new features. Exchange Server Subscription Edition (SE) is now the only supported on-premises Exchange, and there will be no more major versions after it. SE does not receive the features developed for the cloud. Even its first cumulative update has slipped from late 2025 to an undetermined date in 2026.
- The new Outlook does not support it. Microsoft’s own documentation for the new Outlook for Windows says it plainly: “On-premises Exchange accounts aren’t supported.”
- The APIs are moving to the cloud. New functionality ships only on Microsoft Graph, a cloud API. Exchange Web Services in Exchange Online started being switched off in October 2026 and will be gone entirely in April 2027.
None of these steps forces anyone to move on its own. Together, they leave an Exchange administrator with a shrinking set of choices: keep running a server that will not grow, or move the organisation’s mail into Microsoft’s cloud.
For many organisations the second option is not acceptable. Email is the record of a company’s contracts, negotiations, legal advice, HR matters and customer data. Placing it with a US provider means placing it within reach of US law, including the CLOUD Act, which allows US authorities to compel American providers to hand over data they control wherever it is stored. Public administrations, healthcare providers, law firms, defence contractors and many European companies cannot accept that, or no longer want to. Data sovereignty means that you decide where your data lives, under which jurisdiction, and who can read it. A mail service in someone else’s cloud cannot offer that, and an on-premises server whose vendor is steering its customers toward that cloud offers less of it every year.
Outlook without Exchange
Section titled “Outlook without Exchange”
The obstacle to leaving Exchange has rarely been the server. It has been the client.
Many people have spent their whole working life in Outlook. They have years of muscle memory in it: their folder layout, their rules, their calendar views, their shared mailboxes, the way they book meeting rooms. Many organisations also have workflows built around it, such as delegated calendars managed by an assistant. Replacing Exchange with a standard IMAP and CalDAV server has always meant telling every one of those users to switch to a different mail client, or to reconfigure Outlook into a reduced IMAP mode where calendars and contacts no longer sync. For a migration project, that is often where the plan dies.
With Stalwart 1.2.0 the users do not need to change anything. The administrator moves the mailboxes and points the DNS records at Stalwart, and users connect with the same Outlook they used before.
Supported protocols and clients
Section titled “Supported protocols and clients”
Stalwart implements the following Microsoft protocols, all served on the same HTTPS port as JMAP and the WebUI:
- MAPI over HTTP (EMSMDB and NSPI), the native protocol of classic Outlook for Windows, in both cached and online mode. It covers mail, calendars, contacts, tasks and notes, incremental synchronisation, the global address list and the offline address book, delegate access, shared mailboxes, rules, junk email settings, reminders, search folders and read receipts.
- Exchange Web Services, schema versions Exchange 2010 SP2 to Exchange 2016: mail, calendars, contacts, tasks, folders, sharing and delegates, free/busy, inbox rules, out of office, name resolution, distribution lists, and streaming and pull notifications.
- Exchange ActiveSync 14.1 and 16.1: mail, calendars, contacts, tasks and notes, with push through Ping, meeting responses, search and out of office.
- Autodiscover in its POX, SOAP and JSON dialects, so clients configure themselves from an email address and a password.
That set of protocols is what the following clients use to talk to an Exchange server, and they can connect to Stalwart the same way:
- Classic Outlook for Windows (Outlook 2016 and later, including Microsoft 365 Apps), over MAPI over HTTP and EWS.
- Outlook for Mac, over EWS.
- Apple Mail, Calendar and Contacts on macOS, through an Exchange account over EWS.
- Mail, Calendar and Contacts on iPhone and iPad, through an Exchange account over ActiveSync.
- Android mail apps with Exchange account support, such as Gmail, Samsung Email and Nine, over ActiveSync.
- Thunderbird, with its built-in

The top-25 finishers and ties at the 2026 LPGA Q-Series final qualifying stage have been awarded LPGA Tour status for 2027; Megha Ganne won the event outright, while Megan Khang - part of Team USA for the past five Solheim Cups - is one of 27 players to claim a tour card for next season
Monday 23 November 2026 23:16, UK
Megha Ganne won the 2026 LPGA Q-Series final qualifying stage as 27 tour cards were claimed for the 2027 season, with five-time USA Solheim Cup team member Megan Khang among those successful.
Khang - part of Team USA for the past five Solheim Cups - is returning to the LPGA Tour, on which she's made 259 starts since 2016, winning the 2023 CPKC Women's Open.
The top-25 finishers and ties at the conclusion of the 2026 LPGA Q-Series final qualifying were awarded LPGA Tour status for next year.
American Ganne won the final stage outright on 23 under, one shot clear of Shannon Tan and Julia Gregg in a tie for second. Min Sun7 Kim was fourth on 21 under and Xiaowen Yin one further back in fifth.
Ganne, the 2025 US Amateur champion, had actually already secured her 2027 LPGA Tour status by entering the week by finishing 11-15 on the Epson Tour.
Gregg, who finished in a share of second, has never previously had a start on the LPGA Tour.
"It feels unreal," the 25-year-old American said after clinching her place. "It's been my dream since I was four years old to play on the LPGA and now that I finally did it."

The WTGL season continues on Wednesday when Lottie Woad's Boston Common chase their first win of the campaign against Charley Hull's Atlanta Drive GC. Live coverage begins on Wednesday from 1am on Sky Sports Golf.

Appearing on Stephen A. Smith’s radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Hua
items.text:
After Nvidia’s board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Appearing on Stephen A. Smith’s radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Huang would “end up on his feet.”
Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang
Trump got his wish to reinstate Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia — but investigations are still looming.
Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang
Trump got his wish to reinstate Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia — but investigations are still looming.
“You know the expression, anybody can be replaced,” Trump said, floating Apple’s ex-CEO Tim Cook as a potential CEO candidate.
It didn’t take long for Trump to begin softening his approach, making it clear he’d welcome Huang back into the role of CEO even if Nvidia’s own board wasn’t ready to do so. Behind the scenes, the Trump administration was working to grease the landing for Huang’s return. And soon, Nvidia’s board changed its tune: Barely a week after insisting they all agreed to shut the door on Huang’s return, they voted unanimously to reinstate him as CEO, president, and board director.
“There’s nothing wrong with a comeback,” Trump said in a celebratory call to CNBC.
Trump then posted an image on Truth Social of Huang transposed onto Trump’s own body in the infamous photo of him raising his fist after being shot at a campaign rally. In his raised fist, Huang-on-Trump’s-body is clutching a scarlet bra, holding it high in the air.
“There’s nothing wrong with a comeback”
Even after a decisive blow to the president’s power as Democrats swept the midterm elections, Trump appears to maintain his position as a corporate kingmaker. Trump said he spoke with Huang the night prior to his reinstatement and had been in communication with the board both “directly and indirectly.” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement that “President Trump was totally involved” in the board’s decision — Trump decided near the end of last week that he wanted to lead efforts to get Huang reappointed, per The New York Times, so he asked Vice President JD Vance to act as a liaison between Huang and Nvidia’s board, providing reassurances that the move wouldn’t pose a security risk. Trump also reportedly dialed into Nvidia’s Sunday night board meeting to make the case for his return. “I made the deal,” he told CNBC on Monday.
News of Huang’s reappointment, nearly as dramatic as Sam Altman’s return to his CEO role after being voted out by OpenAI’s board in 2023, was a widespread shock to experts, analysts, and investors, particularly after Nvidia’s board had assured stakeholders on its quarterly earnings call last Tuesday that the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On Monday morning, a surge in NASDAQ-100 futures hit a circuit-breaker limit and caused a halt in trading over the volatility.
Trump has meddled in other messy incidents, including by repeatedly — and perhaps illegally — extending the deadline for TikTok to complete its sale to a US entity, and, he admitted on Monday, protecting Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Although he said on CNBC that Musk is “80 percent super genius, 20 percent he has other problems,” Trump said it’s important to protect people like him and Huang. “We have to protect our brilliant people because we don’t have enough.”
But the upcoming Democratic-majority Congress could test both Huang and Trump’s influence. As Republicans prepare for an open presidential primary in 2028, at least one potential candidate appears to be breaking with the president in their skepticism of Huang and Nvidia. And Democrats seem eager to probe both Nvidia and the Trump administration.
The past couple of weeks have been tumultuous for Nvidia. Huang admitted he had had an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom some US intelligence officers reportedly believed to be a potential Chinese spy. There were nearly immediate reports of an additional affair with a direct report, as well as an alleged third affair with a second employee. Megaspeed has reportedly also been investigated for a broader attempt to illegally funnel advanced Nvidia chips to China. Huang himself has pushed to open up more chip sales to China, and he reportedly lied to the Nvidia board about his infidelity. He’s scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1st.
The Nvidia board tried to address concerns about Huang in its announcement Monday, writing that members “received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” It made assurances that the independent investigation it had kicked off about Huang and foreign intelligence would “proceed to conclusion” with Huang’s cooperation.
The board also said it had recently formed an entirely new National Security and Export Control Committee “comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks,” which is working with legal counsel and advisers who have national security experience. Nvidia will be hiring for a new C-suite position, the board said: chief compliance officer. The executive will “oversee compliance” across the company and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance committees. “NVIDIA will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries,” the board added.
Still, the reaction to Huang’s return reflects how small the chance of Huang’s return seemed before Trump’s efforts. Although Trump had previously cast doubt on multiple reports that Alice Huang was a spy, The New York Times reported on Sunday that she “kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year.” According to the Times, which cited multiple people with knowledge of

However, after The New York Times reported there was evidence of another affair, this time with an Nvidia execu
items.text:
After the leather-jacketed CEO, president, and co-founder of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, acknowledged an affair with Megaspeed exec Alice Huang, his company initially announced an investigation. However, after The New York Times reported there was evidence of another affair, this time with an Nvidia executive who reported directly to him, a board meeting that night ended with Huang’s resignation, and Nvidia CFO Colette Kress was installed as the new interim CEO.
And then… Huang was back.
In recent years, Nvidia has become a key part of the Trump administration’s AI push, a central figure in negotiations over potential Chinese access to cutting-edge AI hardware, and a company that has used its now $4 trillion-plus market cap to finance other AI companies. Saying it received input “from senior levels of the United States government,” Nvidia’s board announced his return as CEO on November 23rd, less than two weeks after his resignation.
Follow along below for all of the latest updates.
- Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang After Nvidia’s board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Appearing on Stephen A. Smith’s radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Huang would “end up on his feet.” “You know the expression, anybody can be replaced,” Trump said, floating Apple’s ex-CEO Tim Cook as a potential CEO candidate. Read Article >
- Welcome to elite impunity, Jensen Huang I suppose I must issue a hearty congratulations to Jensen Huang. Huang is CEO of Nvidia again, to the surprise of basically everyone except President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance, who made sure it happened. Now, those of us who had some kind of basic education on what a “free market” is might find it objectionable to have the American president strong-arming a major American company. But our billionaire tech overlords care about the “free market” exactly as much as they care about “free speech,” which is to say not at all. Watching Silicon Valley cheer for what is, effectively, a sign of a command economy has certainly been bracing. But then, why would they give a shit? Their only real beliefs are that they should remain rich and above the law. Jensen may not have exchanged emails with Jeffrey Epstein, but he’s squarely at the Epstein table now. Read Article >
- Here’s Trump discussing the Jensen Huang situation on TV for 10 minutes. Trump did the TV circuit this morning to talk up how involved he was in Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia’s CEO on Monday. He said on CNBC that he spoke to Nvidia’s board, adding, “I convinced them.”
- Jensen Huang says he’ll be a ‘better CEO’ as staff applauds his return Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia’s office as CEO today to a crowd of applauding employees who stood and filmed the cofounder’s first moments back. “Thank you all for the second chances. items.summary: It was a record-breaking occasion in more ways than one. items.text:
It was a record-breaking occasion in more ways than one. David Moyes made history for Everton, edging clear of Harry Catterick by overseeing his 593rd game in charge of the club, but calamitous defending ruined the Scot’s evening and defeat to Brentford was inevitable after James Tarkowski received his first red card in 351 Premier League appearances.
Those in Tarkowski’s corner will claim the Everton captain’s tackle on Yehor Yarmoliuk would not have been a foul back in the day. This, though, was not a “game’s gone” moment. Not that sort of player? The reality is Tarkowski’s back catalogue features plenty of orange card tackles, meaning there was always likely to come a time when his luck ran out.
Everton, whose passive performance denied them the chance to go fifth, should not bother complaining about Matthew Donohue’s intervention from Stockley Park after Tarkowski went in on Yarmoliuk with his studs raised late in the first half. It was the defender’s first red since he was playing for Brentford in the Championship and it had no great bearing on the result. Brentford led 2-0 before their former player went off, Keane Lewis-Potter’s third and fourth goals of the season putting them in control, and dominated from start to finish.
Keith Andrews, a young coach who will have done something right if he comes close to matching Moyes’s longevity, revelled in his side moving sixth thanks to an outstanding display. Moyes has been around long enough to know the top flight has rarely been this open but on this evidence Brentford look likelier than Everton to upset the established order. It was a drubbing, a cracking third from Vitaly Janelt followed by Fábio Carvalho making it 4-0 in added time, and made clear that Brentford have the tools to challenge for European qualification.
With Igor Thiago unavailable after his controversial red card against Brighton it fell to Callum Wilson to lead the line for Brentford. Everton were unsettled by Wilson’s movement and were strangely muted. They sat in a low block but were not compact, were careless in possession and did not deal with Brentford’s wing play and midfield interchanges.
Jaidon Anthony, Mikkel Damsgaard and Michael Kayode had chances before Everton cracked. They were caught out by a long ball down the left and were undone when a poor clearing header led to a moment of brilliance from Anthony, the winger’s cushioned touch with the outside of his right foot running for Lewis-Potter to beat Jordan Pickford thanks to a deflection off Jarrad Branthwaite.
Brentford love to make the most of Lewis-Potter’s attacking instincts after converting him into a left-back. He joined as a winger and his runs are always a threat but Everton did not pay close enough attention. They were abysmal in the first half and faced more pressure when Vitaliy Mykolenko conceded a free-kick after losing Dango Ouattara. Damsgaard crossed, Everton were all at sea and Lewis-Potter scored via another deflection, this time off Thierno Barry.
Everton were dour. They sought a lifeline through Harrison Armstrong, Caiomhín Kelleher tipping the midfielder’s shot over, but composure eluded them. Tarkowski, seemingly rattled by the barracking from the home crowd, was off after storming into a challenge Yarmoliuk. The initial call was a yellow but Tarkowski’s boot was high, the follow-through looked cynical and the force was excessive, convincing Craig Pawson to show a red after a VAR review.
“I don’t think you can tackle like that in this day and age,” Andrews said. Moyes was honest, admitting that Tarkowski’s boot was high. “I can see why the decision went against us,” Everton’s manager said.
Everton adjusted after going down to 10, Merlin Röhl going to right-back, and Thierno Barry’s header drew a superb save from Kelleher just before half-time. Brentford had to switch on. They were intense at the start of the second half and Ouattara nodded wide from Damsgaard’s cross.
Moyes had introduced Jack Grealish for Tyrique George. Yet Brentford recognised the threat and killed Everton off when Janelt used his left foot to belt a formidable shot past Pickford from 30 yards.
“We didn’t play well,” Moyes said. “It was really not like us. I’ve got no complaints with the players. They’ve done a brilliant job until now. Tonight’s performance was not excusable.”
Everton were outplayed on every metric. They were lucky Brentford waited so long to score a fourth, Carvalho coming on to round off the humiliation by bundling in a corner from close range.

I suppose I must issue a hearty congratulations to Jensen Huang. Huang is CEO of Nvidia again, to the surprise of basically everyone except President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance, who made sure it happened.
Welcome to elite impunity, Jensen Huang
Consequences are for the poors.
Welcome to elite impunity, Jensen Huang
Consequences are for the poors.
Now, those of us who had some kind of basic education on what a “free market” is might find it objectionable to have the American president strong-arming a major American company. But our billionaire tech overlords care about the “free market” exactly as much as they care about “free speech,” which is to say not at all. Watching Silicon Valley cheer for what is, effectively, a sign of a command economy has certainly been bracing. But then, why would they give a shit? Their only real beliefs are that they should remain rich and above the law. Jensen may not have exchanged emails with Jeffrey Epstein, but he’s squarely at the Epstein table now.
The deal was reportedly brokered by Peter Thiel’s very own boy
I have argued here, in the past, that the Epstein case laid bare the real politics of the revanchist American right wing: total elite impunity. Well, here it is again! If you are close enough with Trump, it doesn’t matter if you may have jeopardized national security by fucking an alleged Chinese spy. You won’t even be investigated for it before the American president calls in to your board of directors’ meeting to demand you be reinstated. I mean, it is the era of gangster tech regulation — what were any of us expecting? The deal was reportedly brokered by Peter Thiel’s very own boy, Vance.
Just so we can be absolutely clear about what transpired at Nvidia, let’s quickly go through the facts as we know them. A Chinese citizen named Alice Huang acquired the company she renamed Megaspeed, the Singaporean data firm at the center of this inquiry, in 2023. At some point, Huang met Huang, and the two were seen together at a dinner that December. From 2024 to 2025, Megaspeed received more than 200 Nvidia shipments.
In September 2025, the US government began investigating Megaspeed for possible violations of chip export controls; that October, the State Department told Trump of Jensen Huang’s affair with Alice Huang, who was described as a Chinese intelligence asset. Also in October, The New York Times first reported on Megaspeed’s relationship with Nvidia. In December, Trump — who has a close relationship with Jensen Huang — allowed Nvidia to sell more powerful chips to China. In March 2026, Marco Rubio warned the government about Alice, and Trump nonetheless invited Huang to a visit in China. In October, The New York Times reported on the affair. Shortly after Huang sent a note to Nvidia admitting to it, several other reports of infidelity — this time with Nvidia employees — surfaced. On November 12th, Huang resigned. On November 17th, during the Nvidia earnings call, the board’s chair said that the company “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On November 23rd, Huang was back.
This level of open corruption is genuinely impressive
What changed between last week and this week? A week was not enough time to truly review all the information on Huang and his paramour, Alice “No Relation” Huang, the international woman of mystery. The explanation seems to be that Nvidia’s board succumbed to a pressure campaign from Huang’s fellow billionaires, and a direct intervention from the president and vice president of the United States of America.
Sure, all these CEOs ostensibly wanted Huang back at Nvidia to keep the AI trade going. Still, watching the likes of Epic CEO Tim Sweeney, former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick, investing loudmouth Bill Ackman, and Elon Musk — who actually did appear in the Epstein files, and who seemed to be pretty friendly with Epstein! — pitch a fit last week was instructive. These men worried that they might be punished for wrongdoing, that they did not get big enough to be above the law. They have now been reassured, and I suppose that is what really matters. After all, Trump said on CNBC that he gave Nvidia’s board assurances that Jensen is “absolutely fine.”
This level of open corruption is genuinely impressive, and not just because Huang is CEO of Nvidia again. Almost in passing, Trump noted that he had “protected” Musk in his first term from “a certain incident [that] took place, a very tough incident.” In his own inimitable style, Trump told Jim Cramer, “You wouldn’t have Elon if it wasn’t for me.” Surely there is no possible downside when the CEOs of two of the biggest corporations on Earth owe their jobs to Trump personally.
Surely there is no possible downside when the CEOs of two of the biggest corporations on Earth owe their jobs to Trump personally
One thing that has perhaps emboldened this crew is the stance from professional politics-knowers — and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries — that holding members of the Trump administration accountable might be a hindrance to governing. That accountability was part of the reason for the blue wave in November seems to have bypassed these pundits (and the presumptive House majority leader). But then, why should we believe that Democrats will thoroughly investigate this? Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer is claiming to want an investigation, but I am skeptical of how deep that investigation will go as long as Schumer leads it, and only partially because he’s been allied with Silicon Valley for more than a decade. He also has a daughter who works at OpenAI, a company that Nvidia invests in and that is dependent on Nvidia chips. How hard is he really willing to go?
Of course, there may be more to this than just pure economic self-interest. In celebrating Huang’s return, Trump posted a remarkable image. items.text:
For every field, circuits for the Hamiltonian cycle polynomial, and for the permanent outside characteristic 2, need more than m^(c (log m)^(1/3)) gates for all large m. The same holds for approximating circuits. So VP is a proper subset of VNP, and VNP is not contained in the closure of VP. This does not settle P vs NP.
The result was discovered by an internal research Claude model. This folder holds the paper and its Lean 4 formalization. Both were written by AI models, and no human mathematician has checked the proof.
Research artifact. Not maintained and not accepting contributions.
paper.pdf: VP ≠ VNP over every field, by Claude (Anthropic). The full proof is its appendix.
1. Read the statement. Statement.lean states all of the above and imports only Mathlib. Lean checks the proofs, but no machine checks that this file says what is claimed. Appendix Q of paper.pdf lists the Lean counterparts of the numbered statements (Table 3) and says where they differ.
2. Check the proofs. With elan installed, in this folder:
lake exe cache get
lake build
lake env lean scripts/PrintAxioms.lean
The build prints sorry warnings from Challenge.lean only, which states the theorems without proofs for the fuller check. The last command should name no axiom other than propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
The fuller check is the one this repository's CI runs, bash ../.github/scripts/comparator-check.sh (Linux): Comparator compares the statements with Challenge.lean and re-checks the proofs with a second, independently written kernel, nanoda.

Anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship. On Monday, the newly public AI company announced the launch of Claude Ship, a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes.
The latter is th
items.text:
Anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship. On Monday, the newly public AI company announced the launch of Claude Ship, a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes.
The latter is the more interesting part of this new set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now. What’s notable about Claude Ship is not just that it can review proposed code changes and identify and address problems, but that it also includes an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team.
The launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live. With Claude Ship, the idea is to automate even more of the work involved in the development process, essentially by delegating approval authority to an AI agent itself.
“Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” a company blog post explains. “On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code, and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too.”
Claude Ship is launching in beta, allowing early adopters to use it to review pull requests (PRs), and then decide what’s ready to merge.
The new offering consists of Code Review, which is already generally available, and two new agents now in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. PR Steward focuses on addressing issues such as failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and feedback from Code Review. It also comments after every push on what it changed and how to roll it back, if needed.
Claude Approvals then applies an approval policy that the team writes as a file in the repository. This approval process can incorporate various signals, including Code Review findings or the company’s own classifiers, with policies written in natural language.
Because the offering is still in beta, Anthropic suggests running the approval functionality in observe-only mode first. Teams can also choose to start with just one repository and set monthly spending limits to have more control over the process.
Anthropic says teams will also still remain in control of where Claude Ship runs, which review settings to use (e.g., Quick, Standard, or Deep), and which changes should be escalated to a human for a decision.
Claude Ship is rolling out to Claude Team and Enterprise plans for repositories on GitHub. Code Review is generally available, while PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in beta.

items.text:
AI investing startup Supertake has an interesting premise: What if your “takes” on the market could make you money without you having to pick stocks yourself? The service lets people turn their ideas into real investment portfolios, using frontier AI models and trading agents.
Now, the company has raised $20 million in seed funding to grow its business. The round was led by venture firm Adjacent (Nico Wittenborn), with participation from Coinbase Ventures and Union Square Ventures (USV). Numerous angel investors also joined, including Nat Friedman, who’s currently head of product at Meta Superintelligence Labs; Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch; renowned product manager Nikita Bier; investor Scott Belsky; and Nemil Dalal, a former Coinbase exec who is now a visiting partner at Y Combinator.
Michael Mignano originally incubated the startup at USV. He is the co-founder and former CEO of the podcasting platform Anchor, which Spotify acquired in 2019 for over $150 million. After leading Spotify’s podcasting business as “Head of Talk” for a few years, he joined the team at Lightspeed as a venture partner, betting on AI companies like Suno and Granola. He also co-founded Oboe, an AI education startup, and joined USV as a general partner in April.
“We really believed there was an opportunity to make investing more democratized…and give everyone and anyone the ability to invest in their own insights and beliefs and ideas,” Mignano said. While he will continue in his role as founder and executive chairman, he’s now brought in a team to run the company day to day.
The team includes co-founders Lincoln Murr (CEO) and John Peterson (CTO). Both joined from Coinbase, where, Mignano notes, they were the heads of AI product and engineering, leading launches like Coinbase advisor, Coinbase for agents, agentic wallets, and others.
The startup arrives as AI continues to make inroads into financial services, but allowing AI to take over people’s actual investments requires a new level of trust. Supertake is betting that people will ultimately be willing to take that leap, given recent improvements in frontier AI models.
Currently, Supertake works with Coinbase and Robinhood, and the company intends to expand to more brokerages over time. The idea is that you can explain, in broad, natural language, what you believe about how the world is going to change, and Supertake’s AI will iterate with you back and forth to turn that idea into a “take” that’s investable.
Under the hood, the startup is leveraging frontier AI technology and tools, combined with its own proprietary software that directs and limits what the AI can do.
Supertake’s users’ ideas are tracked on a leaderboard on the site, so others who agree can invest alongside them. For instance, there’s currently an idea on the leaderboard about looksmaxxing and longevity becoming more of a trend, where the portfolio includes certain pharma and cosmetic companies that could potentially benefit.
For now, these portfolios consist of stock picks, but the team wants to expand the service over time to handle other types of transactions, like shorts, derivatives, perpetuals, long exposure, or even prediction markets — the latter handled through partnerships with companies in that space.
Despite these “takes” seeming like bets on what could happen next in a given market, Murr stresses that this doesn’t make Supertake itself a prediction market.
“We think it’s a novel and very much improved way to create what was previously considered the robo-advisor experience,” he says. “When that came out, it had this amazing vision and direction of allowing people to have digital asset management. We think now is actually the time for that, with AI agents being so widely proliferated.”
“I don’t think this is necessarily a prediction market by any means. The idea of natural language translation into an underlying set of assets feels different in that regard,” he says.
Still, the startup could wade into short-term predictions if a user’s take involves something they believe could happen in the near future, like who might win an election.
“We’re primarily focused on the longer, medium-term holdings today. But that being said, we don’t want to preclude people from building out very hyper short-term strategies that might exist,” Murr adds.
To address people’s concerns over AI managing their money, Supertake’s team says it’s implementing certain guardrails and spend limits. For instance, the AI has no ability to deposit or withdraw funds on a user’s behalf without their explicit consent. There are also drift limits in place so the portfolio stays balanced, plus allow and deny lists (meaning which assets the AI may and may not trade), real-time monitoring for anomalous activity, tools to set trade size limits, and a restriction that keeps agents from seeing the user’s brokerage credentials.
“We view it as somewhat analogous to self-driving cars, actually, where there is a spectrum here of both trust and technological innovations that are happening,” says Murr. “Where a few years ago you may not feel comfortable getting in a car that has lane assist, but today you get in a Waymo, and it’s like nothing. And we think that there’s a very similar progression happening with the agentic finance space, and we’re far further along in the technological spectrum than people think.”
Access to Supertake is still behind a waitlist while in beta, but the founders said they’ve put their money where their mouths are. Murr and Peterson are letting it manage “tens of thousands” and “thousands” of dollars, respectively.
Mignano, meanwhile, says he has Supertake managing “hundreds of thousands” of dollars.
With the new funding, which follows a $2 million pre-seed round, Supertake aims to expand its team in areas like engineering, design, growth marketing, and others. items.text:
Henry Patten ends partnership with Harri Heliovaara to team up with fellow Briton Neal Skupski
Henry Patten and Harri Heliovaara were crowned the best men's doubles team of the year at last week's ATP Finals after winning Wimbledon for a second time in July; the pair have won three Grand Slam doubles titles together but will go their separate ways in 2027
Monday 23 November 2026 22:29, UK
Henry Patten has ended his world No 1 doubles partnership with Harri Heliovaara in shock fashion in favour of teaming up with British compatriot Neal Skupski for 2027.
Patten and Heliovaara celebrated being crowned the best men's doubles team of the year at last week's ATP Finals after they claimed a second Wimbledon success together back in July.
However, in a post on Heliovaara's blog, the Finnish player revealed Patten phoned him on Friday to say their three-time Grand Slam-winning partnership was over - despite a previous agreement they would continue.
"After the trip to Turin, I didn't even have time to get into the holiday mood when the weekend took a rather unexpected turn," Heliovaara said on his own blog website. "Henry completely unexpectedly announced that he had changed his mind about next year.
"I picked up the kids from daycare on Friday afternoon and we were just opening presents when I got a call from Henry. Without going into too much detail, the message was clear.
"He didn't want to play together again next year, even though we had agreed to do so during the fall. The announcement came as completely as it could come and I couldn't help but listen with my mouth open in horror and say that I don't agree at all.
"I'm unlikely to ever fully understand what and why this ultimately happened.
"The emotional scale in my head was quite violent at first, a shocking situation in any case.
"The two-and-a-half years with Henry have been by far the best time of my career, for which I am eternally grateful to him, but now the main feeling was heavy disappointment and even anger."
Heliovaara confirmed in his blog that he would team up with another British player Julian Cash, while Patten is set to partner Skupski in 2027.

Despite being caught in three affairs — including one with an alleged Chinese spy that has triggered multiple Congressional investigations over national security concerns — Huang was reinstated as CEO and p
items.text:
A handful of tech CEOs, including Elon Musk, are celebrating Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia. Despite being caught in three affairs — including one with an alleged Chinese spy that has triggered multiple Congressional investigations over national security concerns — Huang was reinstated as CEO and president of Nvidia on Monday morning.
“The mistake has been corrected,” Tesla and SpaceX leader Elon Musk wrote on X about Huang’s return.
Musk had been among the most vocal tech leaders to advocate for Huang.
“I think it’s like kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak, and it just doesn’t seem like a good thing for shareholders,” Musk said last week at the DealBook Summit.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman had taken a more neutral stance, commenting last week, “It’s hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen.”
Altman had experienced a similar situation when he was ousted as CEO of OpenAI, then reinstated days later. After the announcement that Huang would return, Altman simply posted, “Jensen!” Many other tech CEOs have similarly refrained from commenting on the matter, given the shifting politics surrounding Huang’s ouster and reinstatement, as well as the national security concerns at the center of the controversy.
In addition to Musk, Binance co-founder and former CEO Changpeng Zhao (CZ), who served prison time for failing to stop criminal activity on the Binance crypto exchange, is also supportive of Huang.
“Glad to see @JensenHuang back,” CZ posted on X with a clapping hands emoji.
Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, who had been among 200,000 signatories on an open letter calling for Huang’s reinstatement, wrote on X, “Jensen’s return will be a demonstration of American resiliency to corporate, political and journalistic missteps.”
Another signatory on the open letter, former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick, who had similarly been driven out of the company he founded after scandals, also voiced his support for Huang on X.
When Nvidia’s stock tanked in reaction to Huang’s ousting, billionaire hedge fund manager Bill Ackman said he believes that the Nvidia board was “not acting in the best interest of shareholders nor in a manner consistent with their fiduciary duties.” As Nvidia’s stock began to rebound Monday morning, Ackman wrote, “The wisdom of the crowd prevails.”
The attitude toward Huang’s return is not as celebratory outside of the tech industry. Across the political spectrum, some elected officials are skeptical about President Donald Trump’s claims that Huang’s return does not threaten national security.
“No national security risk? Based on what?” wrote Senator John Cornyn (R-TX).
Senator Pete Ricketts (R-NB) added, “Nvidia’s decision today doesn’t excuse Jensen Huang from testifying before Congress. It also doesn’t absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips. I look forward to Mr. Huang coming to the Senate in December.”
Huang is still expected to testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3, as well as privately before three House committees.

Brentford 4-0 Everton: Keane Lewis-Potter scores twice as Bees romp past 10-man Toffees
Report and free match highlights from the Premier League clash between Brentford and Everton at the Gtech Community Stadium on Monday night; Keane Lewis-Potter scores twice and James Tarkowski sent off as Bees beat Toffees.
Monday 23 November 2026 22:10, UK
Keane Lewis-Potter’s first-half double set Brentford on their way to a comprehensive 4-0 Premier League win over 10-man Everton.
For David Moyes it was a record-setting night to forget. His 593rd game in charge of Everton, more than any other Toffees manager, ended in misery, as James Tarkowski's red card at 2-0 down left them with no hope of a comeback at the Gtech Community Stadium on Monday night.
- As it happened | Teams | Stats
- Live Premier League table | Watch FREE PL highlights
- Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract on NOW 📺
Vitaly Janelt added a third for Brentford, while Fabio Carvalho came off the bench to score a fourth, as they moved up to sixth in the table, a point above Everton who slipped to ninth.
It was a deserved breakthrough for Brentford midway through the first half. A lovely touch from Jaidon Anthony teed up Lewis-Potter, who saw his strike deflect past Jordan Pickford.
Four minutes later it was 2-0. This time it came from a free-kick as the ball fell to Lewis-Potter. His first effort was blocked, but he got a second bite at it, and again a deflection from his strike took the ball away from the Everton goalkeeper.
It got worse for the Toffees before the break, too. Tarkowski was first given a yellow card for his follow-through challenge on Yehor Yarmolyuk, before a VAR check saw the referee upgrade it to red.
Moyes introduced Jack Grealish at the start of the second half, his first appearance since being dropped from the squad last month, but it would make minimal difference.
Janelt's rocket on 67 minutes added a Brentford third, as he picked out the top corner from 25 yards, while substitute Carvalho prodded in from a corner in stoppage time to add the icing to the cake.
The key moments from the Gtech Community Stadium
19: BIG CHANCE FOR BRENTFORD! Kayode has his head in his hands. The full-back fires wide from inside the box at a slight angle after being played in by Wilson.
22: GOAL! BRENTFORD TAKE DESERVED LEAD! Lewis-Potter's shot from inside the box sneaks past Pickford thanks to a deflection.
26: GOAL! LEWIS-POTTER GETS ANOTHER! That's two goals in the space of four minutes for the Brentford full-back. Both coming thanks to a deflection!.
40: RED CARD! Tarkowski walks. Everton are down to 10.
67: GOAL! Janelt sends a rocket of a shot into the top corner to seal the victory for Brentford. Bosh.
90+1: GOAL! CARVALHO GETS HIS GOAL! It's an instinctive knee into the goal from a couple of yards out from the substitute, who has had such a tough time with injuries.
Story of the match in stats
What’s coming up in the Premier League?
Andrews on high expectations: People need to get real
Brentford boss Keith Andrewsa to Sky Sports:
"[It ranks] really high. It will probably go under the radar because of the sending off but I thought 11 vs 11 we were outstanding.
"We played with bravery, tempo, energy and desire.
"The expectation levels at this club and maybe in the outside world have changed.
"The fact regardless of the performance or result, we win win to go sixth in the league and there is still a little bit swirling in the air: 'we're a little bit unhappy' or 'should they be doing a little bit better'.
"Maybe people need to get a a little bit real. I'm really happy with our group and our football club."
Moyes: It was poor from us
Everton boss David Moyes to Sky Sports:
"I thought Tarky got the ball in plenty of time. He certainly got there before the player who came in late.
"But I think Tarky's foot was high, and in that case then there is a chance it can be given.
"It was very poor from us. A bit unfortunate on a couple occasions that the goals took deflections.
"But that wasn't the reason why we didn't get a result.
"Brentford were better than us on the night and that was it."

The company will be added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List, t
items.text:
Megaspeed, the company that Alice Huang — the woman at the center of the alleged Chinese espionage scandal involving Nvidia — led for over two years, will be placed on a U.S. Commerce Department blacklist, Semafor reported Monday.
The company will be added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List, the outlet writes. This list “contains the names of foreign parties” subject to certain export restrictions designed to ensure that “sensitive technologies do not fall into the hands of those who would threaten U.S. national security or American citizens.”
Functionally, what this will mean is that U.S. companies will not be able to do business with or sell products to Megaspeed without first gaining a special license from the federal government. Semafor cites anonymous sources familiar with the matter to note the move is designed to stop the company “from obtaining US-made semiconductors.”
Megaspeed is a Singapore-based cloud and AI infrastructure provider that, during the period that Nvidia’s boss Jensen Huang self-admittedly had an affair with Huang, was one of Nvidia’s biggest chip customers. Last week, the Commerce Department also announced it had launched a criminal probe into the company. Authorities in both the U.S. and Singapore are now probing whether the company defied export restrictions and illegally smuggled Nvidia chips to China. The company has denied wrongdoing.
TechCrunch reached out to the Commerce Department for comment on the reporting and will update this story if it responds.
After lobbying from President Trump, Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO on Monday after a short period in which he was ousted by the company’s board over the scandal involving Huang.

items.title: AI data centers throw another wrench into chaotic UN climate talks
items.summary: The clean energy revolution hinges on electrifying the entire global economy just as power-hungry data centers are surging. It’s a challenge delegates from all over the world had to grapple with during the United Nations climate conference, called COP31, that came to a chaotic and unsatisfying close
items.text:
The clean energy revolution hinges on electrifying the entire global economy just as power-hungry data centers are surging. It’s a challenge delegates from all over the world had to grapple with during the United Nations climate conference, called COP31, that came to a chaotic and unsatisfying close in Antalya, Turkey, on Sunday.
AI data centers throw another wrench into chaotic UN climate talks
Global climate negotiations fell apart as delegates tried to tackle AI’s growing carbon footprint.
Each year, attendees try to make good on the commitment to stop climate change as part of the 2015 Paris climate accord. Preventing extreme weather from growing more terrifying, coastal communities from flooding, and droughts from wrecking food and water systems requires slashing greenhouse gas emissions. But in order to power homes or cars with solar and wind instead of oil and gas, they need to go electric.
“Every climate minister in the world is thinking about this”
To that end, one of the most anticipated outcomes of this year’s negotiations was a deal to raise electricity’s share of global energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035, compared to about 20 percent today. That becomes harder to do, however, when data centers are causing electricity demand to skyrocket. That made the rush of new AI data centers a climate issue alongside talks on how to transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy.
“Every climate minister in the world is thinking about this, and it will inevitably come up in the discussions. It’s part of the broader energy transformation,” Chris Bowen, Australia’s minister for climate change and energy and the president of COP31 climate negotiations, told Politico in an interview at the start of the COP31 summit.
Despite becoming the longest COP yet, with debates lasting two days longer than scheduled, official negotiations fell apart spectacularly. Delegates ultimately failed to garner enough support to pass the “pact” they’d been bargaining on for two weeks. The EU, UK, and several smaller nations most vulnerable to climate change rejected the deal that they saw as too weak. The pact omitted the term “fossil fuels” despite many nations calling for stronger commitments to phase out oil, coal, and gas. And the US, the epicenter of the data center buildout and the biggest climate polluter historically, was a no-show after the pro-fossil-fuel Trump administration pulled the country out of the Paris accord (twice).
With official negotiations falling apart, and countries only making voluntary commitments on AI and electrification, some environmental and humanitarian groups called this year “the worst COP” ever.
To meet the Paris goals, nations will need to cut their greenhouse gas emissions roughly in half by 2030 before reaching net zero by the middle of the century. Many tech companies made similar commitments in recent years, including Google, Microsoft, and Meta. But thanks to the AI boom, those goals have fallen by the wayside.
Meta is “re-evaluating” its timeline to reach net zero emissions as it focuses on AI, the company said in its annual sustainability report on Thursday. Meta reported a 45 percent year-over-year increase in climate pollution. Google’s and Microsoft’s carbon footprints are also growing despite climate commitments the companies have made. Data centers’ electricity consumption is forecast to double by 2030, according to a forecast by the International Energy Agency.
“That is a huge climate risk: rising power demand from data centres is not yet sustainable, and an AI boom cannot be allowed to become a fossil fuel boom,” Bruce Douglas, CEO of the Global Renewables Alliance, tells The Verge in an email. Data centers were “a key topic” at COP31, according to Douglas, whose organization cohosted a panel on the challenges during the event.
In the US, the country with the most data centers, power sector emissions could increase 42 percent by 2030 as energy companies build more fossil fuel infrastructure to meet data center electricity demand, according to a recent analysis by the Sierra Club. Already, hyperscale data centers in the US create more climate pollution than the country of Denmark, a separate study by Harvard researchers recently found.
To stop data centers from creating more pollution, they would need to be powered by additional new sources of renewable energy, Douglas says. He adds that data centers are currently competing with everyone else for grid connections, finance, and electricity generation capacity — and against arguably more essential tasks like heating and air conditioning, as well as electrifying transportation.
Many tech companies match their electricity use with renewable energy purchases. But unless they’re helping to build new sources of green energy to meet their added electricity demand, they might just end up hogging limited renewable energy capacity. And if more fossil fuels make up the difference, then greenhouse gas emissions continue to rise overall.
“Should new green electrons be used for air-conditioning, electrification or data centres?”
“In many cases, datacentres are outbidding other consumers to get speed to power,” Douglas says. “Should new green electrons be used for air-conditioning, electrification or data centres?”
There was some progress. Around 80 nations signed onto a voluntary pledge to increase electricity’s share of energy consumption to 35 percent over the next decade, according to COP31 president Murat Kurum. The list of countries that includes, however, hasn’t been published yet, Carbon Brief reports.
Another voluntary pledge to keep AI from derailing climate action by calling on data centers to run on less polluting energy also failed to garner much support. Douglas notes that by using the term “low-emission energy,” the pledge still leaves the door open for natural gas (which produces less carbon pollution than coal when burned but is a significant source of methane pollution) to keep powering data centers.

De Bruyne's feelings for Man City will 'never change'

Kevin de Bruyne says his feelings for Manchester City will "never change" even if the club are stripped of their titles after being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules.
De Bruyne, 35, enjoyed a trophy-laden
items.text:
De Bruyne's feelings for Man City will 'never change'
- Published
Kevin de Bruyne says his feelings for Manchester City will "never change" even if the club are stripped of their titles after being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules.
De Bruyne, 35, enjoyed a trophy-laden decade at Etihad Stadium, lifting 16 trophies including the Treble in 2023 before leaving on a free transfer to join Napoli in 2025.
The Belgian returns to City for the second time on Tuesday when Napoli play them in the Champions League.
De Bruyne says he has "nothing but affection" for the club and that "will never change" even if City were forced to give up their domestic titles.
"Of course, it's a lot of things that's been going on but I cannot change anything about that. I am proud of what I have done as a football player and, honestly, this is my club," he said.
"I love the owners, I have talked about a lot of stuff outside football - I have even spoken to [chairman] Khaldoon [Al Mubarak] about how to buy a club."
City deny any wrongdoing and are appealing the decision.
In September it was revealed that an independent commission found that City had arranged "sham contracts" with a number of commercial partners as part of a scheme to disguise secret funding of more than £830m.
- How does Maresca fix City's midfield conundrum? 
  - Published10 hours ago
- Did Cherki's arrival restrict Anderson? 
  - Published14 hours ago
'Everybody plays on the limits'
City await any sanctions that may be imposed following their guilty verdict, with possible punishments ranging from a hefty fine, points deductions, relegation from the Premier League and being stripped of titles.
Asserting its innocence, City said it had filed "a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence [that] exists in support of all of its positions" on 2 October.
Sources have told BBC Sport that City were expected to claim that key sponsorship deals were funded by the Abu Dhabi government, rather than the club's owners, as part of an appeal.
Criticism of City has been intense, but De Bruyne said he can't "change anything" about people calling his former club a "disgrace".
"Of course, in life there are rules, but everybody plays on the limit, I would say, and for me, I played in between the white lines," he said.
"I don't think a lot of people will change in their mind how they view me as a player, or how we played, but everybody has their own opinion."
De Bruyne will be afforded a generous ovation when he returns to Etihad Stadium, having played more than 400 games for City, scoring 108 goals.
After his final home game for the club in May 2025, it was announced that a statue will be built in his honour outside the stadium.

items.title: The 2035 Women’s World Cup has huge potential for women and girls in UK
items.summary:
The announcement that the 2035 Women’s World Cup will be hosted in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland has finally come and, if we aim high enough, it could have a massive societal impact.

items.text:
The announcement that the 2035 Women’s World Cup will be hosted in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland has finally come and, if we aim high enough, it could have a massive societal impact.
Confirmation was a foregone conclusion – the UK was the only bidder – but that did not mean the submission was complacent or lacked ambition.
This tournament, which will be the largest single-sport event staged in the UK, has the potential to transform women’s football in the four host nations and leave a positive wider imprint.
Andy Burnham said as much in his statement after the announcement, saying it “will reach into communities across the country, bring more people into the game and leave a legacy that lasts long after the final whistle”.
In a world where the manosphere is having an increasingly negative and misogynistic influence on young boys and men, the potential impact of a Women’s World Cup on home soil cannot be underestimated.
It is a large-scale problem. A Guardian article in March highlighted that almost a third of Gen Z men and boys think a wife should obey her husband. A 2025 Movember report found that 63% of young men watch masculinity influencers. In September 2023, a YouGov report found that one in six boys aged six to 15 had a positive opinion of Andrew Tate.
The task for the next eight and a half years, and beyond the tournament, is to ensure the 2035 Women’s World Cup isn’t just a great elite football event but that its impact far beyond is maximised.
“So many people in our country are so connected to football,” said Sue Day, the Football Association’s director of women’s football. “I think we can show the country what women and girls can do and it can almost change the narrative a little bit around gender equality.
“It really can have an impact to the benefit of everyone – boys and men as well as women and girls – because there’s so much in that manosphere space that really doesn’t benefit men and boys just as much as it really doesn’t benefit women and girls.
“On the broadest level, my hope, my aspiration and my belief is that something like this touches the lives of everyone in the country. It shows everyone in the country a different way of doing gender roles.”
It is impossible to predict what scale of change the 2035 Women’s World Cup could inspire, but the scope of the bid reflects lessons learned after England hosted the 2022 Women’s Euros. Then, there was a feeling the FA underestimated the level of growth the women’s game would experience between the bid and the tournament.
Old Trafford was a late addition as host of the opening match, a response to increased interest as the tournament moved nearer. The decision to include four stadiums with capacities of less than 20,000, including Manchester City’s 4,400-seat Academy Stadium and the 7,800-seat Leigh Sports Village, was widely criticised. Of 10 host stadiums in 2022, only Wembley and Old Trafford held more than 33,000.
For the 2035 World Cup, 15 of the 22 stadiums in the bid have a capacity of more than 33,000, and 12 exceed 50,000. The list will be trimmed to about 16, but the decision to have stadiums with much bigger capacities to choose from reflects the need to avoid underestimating where the game will be then and the massively increased interest clubs and councils have in hosting the showpiece women’s tournament. It is also a recognition of the financial and commercial benefits the tournament should bring.
The gravitas of the stadium profiles adds to the broader societal impact this World Cup can have: put it in your biggest and best stadiums, have clubs show they believe in the value of women’s football, and fans will do the same.
It is hard to measure the impact the 2022 Euros in England, and the Lionesses’ historic win, had on views of women’s football in the country or the extent to which that tournament challenged misogynistic ideas and attitudes about women and their place in society. There are things that hint towards a shift in consciousness in both instances, though.
In 2022 it wasn’t until the tournament began that it caught the attention of the wider public. In many respects the buildup flew a little under the radar. By the time England’s defence of their title came around in 2025, it felt as if the wider public were invested in the tournament far earlier, knew the players, and were ready to engage.
Before 2035 there are two Women’s World Cups – next summer’s in Brazil and the 2031 tournament in the US, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica – and the UK nations have a chance to qualify for two Euros. That is a lot of top tournament football to inspire growth and fandom and for the 2035 organisers to build on.
“It will be the most amazing tournament,” Day said, “but it’s also a catalyst for growth and inspiration and something to springboard from. I think we can change the world a little bit with the tournament and we should aim that high. Why wouldn’t we aim that high?”

items.text:
Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia’s offices on Monday to an applauding crowd of hundreds of employees, according to several videos circulating online.
The embattled Nvidia founder had stepped down earlier this month amid a series of scandals — including an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which has triggered multiple Congressional hearings over national security, and two affairs with Nvidia employees — but was reinstated as CEO after pushback from the tech community and an intervention by President Donald Trump.
After basking in chants of his name, Huang briefly addressed the crowd.
“Thank you all for the second chance,” he said. “I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around.”
Over 200,000 people, including around 10,000 current Nvidia employees, had signed an open letter advocating for Huang’s return. Other tech leaders also pushed for Huang’s reinstatement, including Elon Musk, who said last week at the DealBook Summit that letting Huang go is like “kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak.”
Amid this increased scrutiny, however, other reports have depicted a different side to Nvidia’s top exec — one where Jensen is not seen as a beloved leader, but as a brutal bully. Based on decades of court documents and over a dozen interviews with current and former Nvidia employees, The New York Times reported that Huang “used humiliation as a tool” and verbally belittled staff at times.

items.text:
Anthropic is launching some new Claude AI features to help software engineers ship code. As part of a new Claude Ship product being announced today, Claude now can review, fix, and approve pull requests.
Claude AI can review pull requests and ship fixes on its own now
Anthropic is bringing new AI tools to software engineers with Claude Ship.
Engineers have already been able to take advantage of Claude’s code review capabilities thanks to the Code Review feature, which was announced in March and became generally available in October. What’s new alongside Claude Ship are the PR Steward and Claude Approvals agents, which are launching in beta today.
PR Steward “jumps in on failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review, other review tools, or team members” and leaves comments on what it changed, according to Anthropic. Claude Approvals can approve routine changes if an organization’s policy allows it. “Teams can have Claude Approvals consider a variety of signals in its decision-making process, including Code Review findings or their own classifiers using natural language,” Anthropic says.
Claude Ship is now available for Claude Team and Enterprise customers and works with repositories on GitHub.

items.text:
The Jensen Huang era of Nvidia nearly came to an end this month. Huang, who three decades ago co-founded what’s come to be considered one of the most important companies in AI, resigned from his role on November 12th over mounting scrutiny around his alleged affairs. Huang admitted he had been “unfaithful” to his wife and that he “created problems for the board.”
How Jensen Huang ended up as Nvidia CEO again
In the span of less than a month, Nvidia lost and reinstated its CEO.
How Jensen Huang ended up as Nvidia CEO again
In the span of less than a month, Nvidia lost and reinstated its CEO.
Huang’s resignation came after weeks of escalating problems, both personal and professional. First, reporting from The New York Times said he had a “close relationship” with a woman passing intelligence to China. Subsequent reporting said that China’s intelligence agency had enlisted that woman, Alice Huang, then an executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed, to spy on Nvidia’s leader, and that the Singapore-based company was under investigation for potentially smuggling AI chips to China. Stories followed that indicated Huang was having an affair with Alice as well as an Nvidia executive, vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell.
So when Huang resigned less than two weeks ago, the decision seemed final. Even Nvidia’s board appeared unwilling to budge. “The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” board chair Harvey Jones said during an earnings call last week.
But in the days following Huang’s resignation, the founder’s allies — including President Donald Trump — mounted a pressure campaign that brought him back to the company he created and sent Nvidia’s share price rocketing upward, almost as though he had never left.
The campaign in support of Huang began almost immediately after his resignation. A coterie of tech leaders began posting in support of Nvidia’s founder: Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney questioned the motives of journalists who broke the stories about his affairs. Tesla CEO Elon Musk likened Huang’s departure to “kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak.” OpenAI CEO Sam Altman later said on stage, “it’s hard to imagine the AI revolution without Jensen.”
“If I didn’t get involved, you’d probably have a very sad Nvidia for a long time to come,” Trump said.
Meanwhile, some of those tech leaders began questioning aspects of the reporting that led to Huang’s exit. Venture capitalist and former White House AI czar David Sacks cast doubt that Alice Huang was a spy, citing a lack of confirmation from US officials. Trump exacerbated the uncertainty, telling reporters, “I don’t know that she is a spy,” despite reports saying the assessment had relied on US intelligence sources.
Nvidia’s board, meanwhile, found itself in a tough position. The company’s shares crashed following Huang’s departure, and they didn’t pick up even after a rosy earnings report. The board was also scrambling to find a new CEO, something industry analysts speculated would prove exceptionally difficult. Reports indicated that Nvidia was considering hiring Arm CEO Rene Haas and Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji, both of whom already have powerful roles in the chip industry.
Trump quickly warmed up to Huang’s return, too. The president — whose investment accounts traded up to $97 million worth of Nvidia stock since returning to office — initially floated the idea of having former Apple CEO Tim Cook take Huang’s place, before saying that it “certainly isn’t a bad idea” to bring Huang back.
This past weekend, Trump appears to have inserted himself into the situation directly. A report from The New York Times says that Trump asked Vice President JD Vance to work with Huang and Nvidia’s board to “resolve the situation,” while the Trump administration reassured the board that it “did not believe that Mr. Huang himself posed a national security risk.” Semafor reports that Trump even called into Nvidia’s board meeting to advocate for Huang’s reinstatement. Sunday evening, Trump said in a post on Truth Social that he hopes Nvidia’s board “rehires Jensen Huang.”
Hours later, Nvidia’s board did just that. The board announced on Monday that it reinstated Huang as its CEO, president, and board member. In its statement, the board said that it received input “from senior levels of the United States government,” and determined that “Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.”
Trump immediately took credit for Huang’s reinstatement, with White House spokesperson Steven Cheung saying the president “was totally involved” in the decision. “If I didn’t get involved, you’d probably have a very sad Nvidia for a long time to come,” Trump said during an interview with CNBC. He added in a post on Truth Social that the US Attorney General confirmed that it doesn’t have evidence that Huang “engaged in any unlawful conduct.”
Nvidia’s shares rose on the news of Huang’s reinstatement, while tech leaders celebrated his return on social media. But the saga is likely far from over. The board said it will finish its investigation into Huang, the Securities and Exchange Commission is looking into Nvidia’s “accounting practices,” and Megaspeed is being investigated by the Justice Department. Even Trump has said that Nvidia should continue its internal investigation about export controls compliance.
Trump’s apparent involvement also leaves plenty of room for scrutiny from Democratic lawmakers, who will control the House and Senate next year. Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) called Nvidia’s decision “reckless” and urged the Trump administration to explain the “input” government officials provided to the company’s board
Huang’s stunning reinstatement still leaves many questions unanswered. Though the backing of Wall Street, the White House, and Silicon Valley may have brought Huang back as CEO, a new wave of scrutiny from federal regulators and lawmakers is just getting starte

items.title: Are Man Utd genuinely in a relegation battle?
items.summary:
Are Manchester United in a relegation battle? Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher assess their survival chances
After Manchester United's 4-0 thrashing at Liverpool, Mauricio Pochettino's side officially have the worst defence in Europe and have endured their worst start to a season in over half a cent
items.text:
Are Manchester United in a relegation battle? Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher assess their survival chances
After Manchester United's 4-0 thrashing at Liverpool, Mauricio Pochettino's side officially have the worst defence in Europe and have endured their worst start to a season in over half a century - so are they going down?
Monday 23 November 2026 19:56, UK
What started as a blip has become a problem far more systemic for Man Utd.
"If the name wasn't Man Utd and you're watching their performances, you'd say they are a team in a relegation fight. They're conceding lots of goals, a comedy of errors, red cards - they've won one game all season," said Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher.
Only Ipswich beaten in 11 attempts, the worst defence in Europe - and a 4-0 hammering at Liverpool on Sunday to wipe the gloss off Mauricio Pochettino's arrival within 12 first-half minutes.
Carragher added: "This Manchester United back four can't cope with pace. They're a million miles off it in terms of coming up against what they are in the Premier League."
The unthinkable is beginning to become thinkable. Are United in an actual relegation battle now?
