- Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺
"They're in a relegation fight right now because of where they are in the table," said Carragher after a fifth defeat of the season left them with their lowest points tally at this stage of a season since 1972. "You can't say anything else when you look at their record this season.
"We don't believe it will happen over a 38-game season, but they haven't had the most difficult of starts. They've played a lot of promoted teams; they haven't played the best team in the league, Arsenal, yet.
"I don't think they'll go down, but this idea that they haven't got a scrap on their hands, they have."
It seems unfathomable. But should it? The numbers don't give Pochettino any grounds for optimism. Only 26 teams - barely one a season - have picked up eight points or fewer from their opening 11 games in the history of the Premier League and only 13 of those, exactly half, avoided the drop.
Of course, most of those were not clubs anywhere near the size and stature of Manchester United. But even the Opta supercomputer, which provides far more contextualised feedback, is losing faith and gives them a 24 per cent chance of going down - though it does still back them to stumble to safety and finish 16th.
"You wonder how low it can get," said Gary Neville after Sunday's defeat. "It's embarrassing. I don't believe they're in a relegation fight, they'll get out of this, but this is the worst Man Utd have been in 53 years. The worst defensive team in Europe, second-bottom in the league, they've never started this badly.
"Mauricio Pochettino's options aren't great."
That may be putting it lightly. As well as the worst defence in Europe's top-five leagues across all competitions, United also have the third-worst performing attack in the Premier League, falling below their xG tally by 4.2 goals already.
In an immediately infamous tweet in 2014, then-boss David Moyes was quoted as saying United "must improve in a number of areas, including passing, creating chances and defending".
Pochettino is unlikely to admit it publicly, but behind closed doors must have similarly widespread concerns even at this early stage. United have not found themselves in the bottom two after 11 games in 40 years.
Sir Alex Ferguson was brought in as their eventual saviour that winter, but turning the tide on this United side is a significantly bigger ask.
Are there personnel at his disposal who could improve matters? Potentially. Neville did pinpoint a back four of Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez and Diego Dalot who could at least get United out of their defensive slump.
"It's a poor back four, but it's their best back four. It could compete," he added. "But the one that started today and finished against Villa a few weeks ago, that'll get you relegated."
There is good news and bad news. Neville's quartet are unbeaten in every game they have started together since the start of 2023/24 - and can boast a 70-per-cent win ratio. Unfortunately for Pochettino, that only amounts to 10 games across more than three seasons, owing largely to availability.
But that still does not solve the problem of their limp attack. Of the 22 players to have attempted a shot for the club this season, 19 have under-performed their xG, and the three who have not, Benjamin Sesko, Joshua Zirkzee and Youri Tielemans, have scored only a solitary goal apiece.
There remain huge question marks over the Man Utd dressing room, its commitment and a lack of leadership which permeated into the public sphere in the final weeks of Michael Carrick's reign. Though Pochettino's players have shown they can perform when they want to. Carrick himself knows that better than anyone.
But his successor barely has time to address it over the next few weeks, with only one free midweek between now and the end of 2026 - and even then he has a trip to the Emirates, live on Sky Sports on December 20, to face at the end of his first uninterrupted week on the training pitch.
By that point United will be almost half-way through the Premier League season - and alarm bells will be ringing even louder if they still find themselves in the quagmire, especially with rock bottom Crystal Palace and promoted Coventry to come before then.
But might even that prove problematic for Pochettino?
"If you look at the strength of the Premier League this season, in terms of what we would call the teams you'd expect to be mid-table or near the bottom - it's probably as strong as it's ever been," said Carragher.
"There's no poor teams. There's not many great teams, but there's no poor teams.
"And that's a problem for Man Utd."

items.title: Carra: Chelsea must sign centre-back or achieve nothing
items.summary:
Chelsea must sign centre-back or will achieve nothing with Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana, says Jamie Carragher
Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher analysed Chelsea's leaky defence on Monday Night Football, highlighting the partnership of Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana as a major concern; watch Nott'm Fores
items.text:
Chelsea must sign centre-back or will achieve nothing with Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana, says Jamie Carragher
Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher analysed Chelsea's leaky defence on Monday Night Football, highlighting the partnership of Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana as a major concern; watch Nott'm Forest vs Chelsea on Friday, live on Sky Sports; kick-off 8pm
Monday 23 November 2026 20:07, UK
Jamie Carragher believes Chelsea must sign a dominant centre-back or they will have "no chance of achieving anything".
Chelsea have conceded 20 goals in 11 Premier League games this season and were thrashed 4-1 at home to Leeds on Saturday, which has put pressure on new manager Xabi Alonso, with his side sitting eighth and already 12 points behind leaders Arsenal.
Leeds overpowered Chelsea with their physicality, as Dominic Calvert-Lewin bullied centre-backs Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana, exposing their weak defence the same way Sunderland's Brian Brobbey did in their 1-0 win before the international break.

Chelsea are five points behind fourth-placed Liverpool and are already without European football this season - but Carragher feels qualifying for the Champions League will be a difficult task with their current centre-back pairing.
"Chelsea have got a massive problem at centre-back and if they don't change it in January, they're going to have a big problem in terms of where they feel they should be this season with the Champions League," he said on Monday Night Football.
"Colwill at Sunderland against Brobbey gave the penalty away, and the manager took him off at half-time. Fofana's performance against Man United, especially in the first half, was one of the worst you'll see from a centre-back this season.
"As a partnership, this will never work because they're not physical enough and there's no real leader there.
"It almost feels like you've got two novices playing, but one cost £75m, and Colwill has been talked up a lot not just at Chelsea but at international level as well."
Chelsea signed centre-back Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace for £51m in the summer, but he has missed the last three matches with a hamstring injury.
"Those two (Colwill and Fofana) can't play in a back four as a two, but it reminds me of myself at Liverpool," said Carragher. "We didn't fix it defensively and we were seen as weak, conceding from set pieces and long throws. It wasn't until we signed Sami Hyypia, 6ft 4in, dominant centre-back, leader, great player, that it changed for us.
"This is not going to change with what they have. Lacroix is a decent player, that's a sticking plaster until the next transfer window in January or the end of the season. Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they've got absolutely no chance of achieving anything."
Chelsea have kept the fourth fewest clean sheets in Europe this calendar year, which largely predates Alonso's tenure, although Carragher has been surprised by the former Bayer Leverkusen and Real Madrid head coach's style.
"There's a lot of talk now about Xabi Alonso and I think watching Chelsea this season, they haven't been that impressive even when they've won games in terms of how I think we all felt they would play," he added.
"Everybody had this idea, myself included, who had watched Leverkusen play, you think of the player Xabi Alonso would play, the Spanish influence and managed by Pep Guardiola. You're expecting Chelsea to be more of a possession-based team and when you watch them the football isn't amazing and they rely on the front three a lot.
"Cole Palmer has dropped off in the last few weeks and Joao Pedro has been injured as well. When they've all been there, it always felt like there was an overreliance on that front three. The goal on the weekend was a direct play; you can get goals in different ways, but there hasn't been that intricate football that we were expecting."
Merson: My worry is that Liverpool thought Alonso wasn't good enough
In his latest Sky Sports column, Paul Merson has raised doubts about whether Alonso is good enough as Chelsea manager after Saturday's home loss to Leeds.
Merson believes Liverpool may have snubbed Alonso for the head coach role - eventually taken by Andoni Iraola - due to concerns about his pedigree.
He told Sky Sports: "My biggest worry is that Liverpool could have had Xabi Alonso and they chose not to. Obviously, Liverpool didn't think he was good enough.
"Alonso took the Chelsea job, and Liverpool sacked Arne Slot two weeks later. You can't tell me that Liverpool couldn't have spoken to Alonso and say: 'Don't take the Chelsea job, we're going to take you'.
"He was out of a job as well, Liverpool could have had him and he'd have gone there all day long. So why didn't they take him? Did they know something that we're seeing now?
"It just always sits in my mind. That was my worry - and now it's playing out.
"If this was Liam Rosenior in charge at Chelsea and getting these results, he'd be in major trouble. One hundred per cent, he'd be in trouble. And remember, Rosenior didn't have Morgan Rogers in his Chelsea team, bought for £116m.
"But it's because of the unbelievable job he did at Bayer Leverkusen that everybody is thinking: it will be alright."

items.title: Google Search’s AI Mode can now tap into Drive and Wallet for more personalized responses
items.summary: Google announced on Monday that it’s expanding Personal Intelligence in Search’s AI Mode with integrations for Google Drive, Google Wallet, and the Gemini app. Personal Intelligence is designed to offer users more personalized, context-aware answers by connecting to their Google apps and drawing on
items.text:
Google announced on Monday that it’s expanding Personal Intelligence in Search’s AI Mode with integrations for Google Drive, Google Wallet, and the Gemini app. Personal Intelligence is designed to offer users more personalized, context-aware answers by connecting to their Google apps and drawing on information from their digital lives. The feature can already connect to apps like Gmail, Google Calendar, and Google Photos.
By bringing Personal Intelligence in AI Mode to Drive, Wallet, and the Gemini app, Google is leveraging the wealth of user data that’s already within its ecosystem. Since users rely on these services, the tech giant can deliver more personalized experiences that rivals aren’t able to match. Of course, not everyone wants AI looking at their Wallet and Drive, so connecting the apps is optional, and you can turn Personal Intelligence on or off at any time.
Google says that connecting Google Wallet to Personal Intelligence lets users track their financial goals, cut everyday spending, and make better use of credit card rewards. The tech giant notes that if users choose to connect their Wallet, AI Mode can only read information from accounts and isn’t able to move or manage their money.
As for Drive, the company says important information related to a project or major decision is often scattered across documents and spreadsheets. By connecting Google Drive to Personal Intelligence, AI can draw on those files to provide more relevant, personalized answers, such as creating a tailored plan for tax season.
Users will also be able to share context between their Gemini app and AI Mode in Search, which means that if they explore an idea in the Gemini app, they won’t have to start over with AI Mode because it will already have the information, and vice versa.
Additionally, Google says users will soon be able to view the context that AI Mode uses via a new “Personalization” icon that will appear below responses.
The company also announced on Monday that users will start to see more personally relevant responses in AI Overviews and AI Mode that will be tailored to users’ recent search context.

items.title: Nothing’s upcoming Ear Note is a pair of earbuds with AI transcription
items.summary: Nothing’s new AI device is the Ear Note, a set of earbuds and their microphone-equipped charging case that can record and transcribe conversations, with a connected app to manage the recordings, transcriptions and AI-generated summaries, similar to Apple’s new Watch feature and devices like Amazon’s
items.text:
Nothing’s new AI device is the Ear Note, a set of earbuds and their microphone-equipped charging case that can record and transcribe conversations, with a connected app to manage the recordings, transcriptions and AI-generated summaries, similar to Apple’s new Watch feature and devices like Amazon’s Bee wearable. Nothing CEO Carl Pei demonstrated the new device to Bloomberg, but said the company hasn’t yet settled on a price ahead of a planned launch on December 8th.
Nothing’s upcoming Ear Note is a pair of earbuds with AI transcription
The new AI device from Nothing can record and transcribe audio with AI from the earbuds or via microphones on their charging case.
The report also says Nothing’s rumored plans for an AI smartwatch and smart glasses are delayed, while it will be “pursuing a more aggressive smartphone release schedule next year than it did in 2026.” In a post on X, Pei said this is “the first of many products building a hardware context layer for AI. Rather than ask you to carry a new product, we took something you already wear and trust and made it intelligent.”
According to Bloomberg, the earbuds will “support interactions with various AI agents, including a more basic voice-control system developed by Nothing, letting users engage in back-and-forth conversations.” Users will also be able to record themselves with a “Talk” button on the case, like Nothing previously included on the Ear 3, which also has recording capabilities. Earlier this year, Nothing introduced an Audio Snapshot recording feature in the Ear 3A. Anker’s Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro Max can also record directly to the earbuds’ case and generate AI transcripts and summaries in an app.

items.summary:
Key events
Before we dig into the teams, here’s Keith Andrews, who acknowledges Brentford’s best start to a Premier League season, but is also frustrated they’ve not got more points – especially after a brilliant pre-season.
On his team, he says the missing Igor Thiago presses superbly from the fron
items.text:
Key events
Before we dig into the teams, here’s Keith Andrews, who acknowledges Brentford’s best start to a Premier League season, but is also frustrated they’ve not got more points – especially after a brilliant pre-season.
On his team, he says the missing Igor Thiago presses superbly from the front, but Callum Wilson wasn’t just signed as a sub and has added a lot to the dressing room. Brentford will tweak their method to account for the change, but won’t alter their essentials.
Back to pre-season, he says he hit on an XI towards the end of it, which is why Mikel Damsgaard hasn’t played much, but he’s a talented player and gets his chance tonight.
Brentford (4-3-3): Kelleher; Kayode, Ajer, Van den Berg, Lewis-Potter; Yarmoliuk, Janelt, Damsgaard; Outtara, Wilson, Anthony. Subs: Valdimarsson, Schade, Jensen, Carvalho, Sangare, Diouf, Nunes, Schuster, Fredrick.
Everton (4-2-3-1): Pickford; O’Brien, Tarkowski, Branthwaite, Mykolenko; Garner, Armstrong, Rohl, Dewsbury-Hall, George; Barry. Subs: Travers, Maitland-Niles, Keane, Grealish, Dibling, Johnson, Norgaard, Alcaraz, Hackney.
Referee: Craig Pawson (Sheffield)
Though the standard at the top of the Premier League reflects neither its spending or self-mythologising, the level below that is perhaps higher than in any league, ever. Every team is organised, physical and athletic, with technical players in pretty much every position and various able to settle a game. As such, only seven points separate Bournemouth, in fifth place, from Ipswich Town, in 16th, results dependent not just on which side is better but who plays whom when, with final positions a reflection of what happens to be happening when the music stops.
Tonight’s match is emblematic of this condition. Only one side in that top 16 – 15th placed Fulham – have scored fewer than Everton’s 12 goals in 10 games yet, somehow, David Moyes’ men are seventh in the table. Brentford, meanwhile, are two points behind in 10th and, outside of the top four, only sixth-placed Leeds have conceded fewer than their 11 goals.
Which is one way of saying tonight’s encounter is unlikely to deliver a goal-fest. But, on the other hand, it will give us two focused, settled, confident sides, fuelled by intensity, skill and just a little bit of magic.
Kick-off: 8pm GMT

For those who don't know me, let me introduce myself. I'm the independent developer behind FSNotes, an open-source note-taking app for macOS and iOS.
I've been developing FSNotes for 9 years. And what happened a few weeks ago came as a complete shock.
Apple removed my app from every European App Store. Without a clear explanation or any way to resolve the issue promptly.
It all started when I didn't receive my October sales payout. This had happened before, but I was usually able to resolve it by contacting Apple Support. Not this time.
I opened two support cases:
- November 5 — Case ID: 23353628
- November 17 — Case ID: 23573022
Since November 5, I haven't received a single response. Not one.
I've gone through everything I could find in App Store Connect, completed the necessary compliance information under the EU Digital Services Act (DSA), and submitted official documents from Ukraine's government business registry.
I'm a legally registered sole proprietor in Ukraine. I run my business officially and pay my taxes. But apparently, that's not enough. Or perhaps nobody is even reviewing my documents.
And you know what's the most frustrating part?
While Apple remains silent, everything I've spent nine years building is being destroyed.
My app is losing its positions in App Store rankings and search results. The visibility, reputation, and discoverability I've worked so hard to build over the years are disappearing right before my eyes.
Even if Apple restores my app tomorrow, who's going to give me those rankings back? Who will compensate me for the lost time, users, and revenue?
I'm not asking for special treatment. I'm not asking Apple to bend the rules for me. I simply want someone to review my documents, explain the restrictions, and give me a chance to resolve the issue.
It's especially painful to see how difficult it has become for a Ukrainian developer to keep working. Sometimes it feels like Ukraine is the country under sanctions, not Russia.
FSNotes is still available for free on GitHub. I'll continue providing access to the source code and free builds. But the reality is that without revenue, it will be extremely difficult for an independent project like this to survive.
I'm asking you to support this open letter to Apple with a like or a repost. I'm not asking for donations or special privileges. I just want to bring this situation to the attention of the App Store team.
You cannot simply remove an app with a nine-year history from sale, ignore a developer's support requests for weeks, and provide no explanation of what's happening.
This kind of treatment is killing indie development.

items.text:
Marco Penge claims maiden PGA Tour win: Englishman triumphs from four-way playoff at RSM Classic
Three-time DP World Tour winner Marco Penge was in danger of losing his PGA Tour card after a 2026 season disrupted by a viral illness; the 28-year-old Englishman secures his card in stunning fashion with his maiden triumph at year-ending RSM Classic in thrilling four-way playoff finish
Monday 23 November 2026 20:17, UK
English golfer Marco Penge claimed a stunning maiden win on the PGA Tour as he emerged victorious from a four-way playoff at the season-ending RSM Classic.
Penge, a three-time winner on the DP World Tour, had gone into the tournament at risk of losing his PGA Tour card for next year after a rookie season disrupted by a viral illness placed him outside of the top 100.
With a top-four finish required to retain his spot, the 28-year-old found form at the best possible time at the Sea Island Golf Club this week, and a final-round 65 earned him a spot alongside Haotong Li of China and Americans Michael Thorbjornsen and Max Greyserman in a playoff decider - all four locked at 16 under.
- The RSM Classic: Latest leaderboard [external]

Penge's five-under 65 on the Seaside Course included six birdies, including one at the last, and a single bogey, while he birdied 18 again to clinch victory in the playoff after nailing his approach to 10 feet.
"I always seem to play my best golf when my back's up against the wall," Penge said following his stunning win.
"I've been through this before on the DP World Tour, keeping my card in the last event and dealing with adversity and coming back from health issues, all that stuff.
"So I knew I could do it, I just wasn't sure I ever had the game this week to be able to do it and thankfully I did."
Rasmus Hojgaard, who had held a share of the lead - on 13 under with Thorbjornsen - heading into the weather-delayed final round on Monday, ultimately finish tied fifth.
The Ryder Cup star posted a disappointing final round of 69 to end two shots off the pace on 14 under, level with Jackson Koivun.
Fellow Americans Harris English, Nick Dunlap and five-time major winner Brooks Koepka finished tied-seventh, ninth and tied-10th, respectively.
Denmark's Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen also finished in the top 10.

Max Verstappen and George Russell: Has feud reignited at wrong time for Mercedes driver after difficult 2026 F1 season?
The feud between George Russell and Max Verstappen reignited in spectacular style in Las Vegas following a clash between the pair in practice; watch the Qatar Grand Prix live on Sky Sports this weekend, with qualifying at 6pm on Saturday and the race at 4pm on Sunday
Monday 23 November 2026 18:44, UK
The reignition of the long-running feud between George Russell and Max Verstappen has added an entertaining twist to the end of the 2026 Formula 1 season, but it may not be what the Mercedes driver needed at this moment.
Russell and Verstappen clashed during final practice at the Las Vegas Grand Prix when the Red Bull driver, slightly cheekily, snatched track position from his Mercedes rival as they both prepared for push laps.
Irked by Verstappen's actions, which he later said he felt breached a gentleman's agreement the drivers share, Russell attempted to reclaim track position from the weaving Red Bull, with the pair making slight contact.

The stewards summoned the two drivers following the session as they conducted an investigation, before handing Verstappen a warning.
The incident came less than a month on from Verstappen being involved a similar incident with Racing Bulls driver Liam Lawson during practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix, which resulted in both drivers being given one-place grid penalties.
Speaking to Sky Italy later that evening, Russell said: "There's nothing in the rules to say you cannot overtake someone who is starting a lap but when you do this, you are screwing this person over and he does this week in, week out with many drivers and everybody accepts it.
"I'm not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they're bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody's got to stand up to that guy."
Russell's comments came after the result of qualifying in Las Vegas dictated that the pair would start together on the front row, with Verstappen ahead in pole position.
That setup a Saturday night showdown, in which the pair engaged in a thrilling battle for the lead for much of the race, before Russell dropped behind Kimi Antonelli in the latter stages and then drove into a barrier attempting to pass his Mercedes team-mate.
Verstappen reacted on team radio with apparent glee having seen Russell's error in his mirrors, and then, after closing out a superb victory, further stuck the boot into the British driver during the post-race press conference for the top three.
The four-time world champion said: "The thing is, he speaks a lot next to the track. And honestly, for me, it doesn't really bother me because he's so far below my level that it doesn't really make any sense for me anyway to try and challenge that. So, it doesn't bother me.
"And today, karma is a b****. It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror and I saw what was happening [when Russell crashed]. I was like, 'fantastic, my day is only getting better.' And of course, when I then crossed the line in first, my day was complete."
A history of the Russell-Verstappen feud
With less than five months separating them in age, Russell and Verstappen have been racing each other in karting since they were children.
While Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff reflected in Las Vegas that the feud may have stretched back to those days, the first notable F1 flashpoint between the pair came in the 2023 Azerbaijan Sprint when they made contact through several corners on the opening lap.
In a post-race exchange broadcast to the world, Verstappen barked at Russell to "expect next time the same" and swore at the Mercedes driver as he walked away. He would later refer to Russell as "princess George" in an interview with the Dutch media.
A spectacular fall out between the pair then occurred towards the end of the 2024 season, after Verstappen felt Russell had played an unreasonably key role in the Red Bull driver being given a grid penalty that cost him pole for the Qatar Grand Prix.
Verstappen said in Qatar that he had "lost all respect" for Russell, who then responded with a remarkable explosive verbal attack on the Dutchman the following week at the season-ending Abu Dhabi Grand Prix.
Russell said Verstappen had threatened to put him "in the wall" in Qatar, and said that "people have been bullied by Max for years". Verstappen questioned the accuracy of Russell's claims and labelled him a "loser" and "backstabber".
The pair clashed once more on track at the 2025 Spanish Grand Prix when Verstappen, enraged at his own team for instructing him to let Russell through to avoid receiving a penalty, appeared to wave the Mercedes past before lunging into the side of it.
Verstappen was penalised by the stewards, later admitted the move was "not right" and apologised to his team, but did not personally address Russell.
Less talked about than the pair's clashes is a potential further tension added by Russell's boss Wolff having very publicly tried to sign Verstappen from Red Bull. Russell told Sky Sports F1 in June 2025 that his own contract extension was being delayed by Mercedes' attempts to sign Verstappen.
More 2026 pain for Russell?
The previous clashes between the pair came when Russell was in a position of strength at Mercedes, given he had performed hugely impressively during his first four seasons with the team from 2022 to 2025.
Russell had expressed belief on many occasions over the years that if Mercedes delivered a title-winning car, he was ready to grab the opportunity, and few doubted him.

Jensen Huang is scheduled to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3, according to a notice on the committee’s website.
The development comes just hours after Huang was reinstated as Nvidia chief executive, less than two weeks following his resignation after it was revealed that he engaged in at least two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected by the U.S. government of working as a Chinese spy.
The Senate Banking Committee has jurisdiction over export control policies that are designed to prevent sensitive U.S. technologies, such as chips capable of powering AI models, from falling into the hands of foreign governments and militaries.
The public hearing follows bipartisan calls for Huang to testify about his affair with the suspected Chinese spy and his potential involvement in chip-smuggling operations.
It’s worth noting that before his reinstatement as CEO, Huang had already agreed to appear before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, and the House Intelligence Committee on December 1.

items.title: Madness erupts as Sevilla deny Betis in wild end to Spain’s ‘derby of derbies’
items.summary: “If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said. Instead, this was madness, the kind of moment a derby is meant to have, even if it has nothing else. It was late, it was lucky, and there wasn’t even a winner but right there, right then, at 24 minutes
items.text:
“If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said. Instead, this was madness, the kind of moment a derby is meant to have, even if it has nothing else. It was late, it was lucky, and there wasn’t even a winner but right there, right then, at 24 minutes past 8pm on Saturday evening in the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium, it felt like there was. Frankly it was a bit rubbish, as bad a goal as you’ll see, but it was also the best, practically Pelé against the Nazis. Suddenly there were arms and legs everywhere, tears too. Cameras confirmed it. Zoom in and there they are: actual, real life tears.
In the 91st minute of the 146th meeting between Sevilla Fútbol Club and Real Betis Balompié – “derby of derbies” according to Luis García, the Sevilla coach for whom it was the first – Salas’s shot from 18 yards went through Marc Bartra’s legs and Álvaro Valles’s hands. The ball dribbled into the Betis net so apologetically it barely touched the net at all and hadn’t got there before Sevilla’s vice-captain was gone. Raised in Morón de la Frontera, to the south of a city divided, Salas joined Sevilla at 11; now, having levelled the game at 1-1, he went tearing towards the terraces, absolutely losing it like they were.
In the six-yard box, Robbie Ure, the Scottish striker who had watched the ball pass and whose own shot barely 100 seconds before was the eighth Betis blocked, resigned to the fact that it just wasn’t going to happen, reacted to the fact that it actually had with his right arm pumping like Animal on the drums. Screaming as he went, Salas thumped at his chest as hard. Around the Sánchez Pizjuán, 42,983 went wild except the 600 Béticos high in the corner. They couldn’t believe this and nor could their players: of all the ways to let go. From the Sevilla bench, everyone ran towards the team.
García went the other way through the crowd in his blue suit, like the final scene of a romcom: a man fighting against the rush-hour tide, bundling into a busy subway station desperate to reach the train before it leaves with her on board. He was in the middle of the pitch when he put the brakes on and returned, alone. He had been through the emotions; frustration, relief, joy, vindication and frustration again. A colleague awaited with a high five that was hard too. They could have won. But they also could have lost – Sevilla had trailed to Antony’s goal, which wasn’t great either, and Odysseas Vlachodimos’s superb save had prevented the Brazilian from getting Betis’s second and ending it – but at least they had salvaged a point.
At the final whistle, the Betis midfielder Dani Ceballos came to console Valles. “You’ve been our best player this season,” he told the goalkeeper, which was true. No one in La Liga has made more saves and none have been more significant either. Valles’s xG avoided is 8.3; the next best is 4.1. At the same time, Salas tried to do the post-game interview but couldn’t hear over the noise. Behind him, his family were waiting for a hug. As Betis’s players made their way, Sevilla’s players stood before supporters at the north end, applauding and applauded back.
“When you go to your greatest rivals’ ground, you deserve to win but they get a draw and on top of that they celebrate it, you know you’re doing things right,” said the Betis captain Bartra, who also claimed that Salas shouldn’t have been on the pitch to score the equaliser after he had trodden on Isco’s ankle. “A bad game from us only allows them to draw at home,” said the Betis president, Ángel Haro. “Fortunately, we’re in a period when a draw feels like sadness to us and a triumph for them.”
And so the debate was served, so the accusations came, the usual nonsense. In Spain? In Seville? Surely not?! Etc and so on. But if the words of Betis’s captain and president prompted that, if those words were a little pointed in a city where they pride themselves on being wind-up merchants and the derby is the most passionate in the country, there is an obvious response: well, yeah. Not least precisely because it’s about putting one over on each other. Every goal is an explosion and Sevilla got theirs in the 91st minute. Against Betis. From the centre-back who’s been at the club half his life. Of course they celebrated it.
If it might have seemed a little odd for Sevilla to stand there before their fans celebrating when they hadn’t won and a run of one win in seven in the league had been confirmed, that too was part of it. Because Bartra and Haro were right, to their credit and to Sevilla’s too. At the start of this derby, a huge banner came down over the north stand; a supporters’ work of art made by hand as ever, it lauded a history of greatness, but maybe history is the word, and that’s the real greatness: it is three years since Sevilla won a trophy or qualified for Europe, those days not just fading fast but long gone, yet here they are anyway, more than 35,000 of them every week.
Sevilla are a club in crisis, where the former president José María del Nido is at war with the former president José María del Nido – and, yes, they are father and son. Where the debt is almost €200m (£167.2m) and the solution, a sale to a consortium led by Sergio Ramos, fell through. Where they have the lowest salary limit in the whole of primera, at €20m (£16.7m), and four second division teams were allowed to spend more. Where this summer they had a net spend of minus €25m (£20.9m). And where they qualified for the Champions League three years running under Julen Lopetegui, sacked him, went through seven managers in three years and finished 12th, 14th and 17th, closer to relegation every season.
In May they finished 13th yet only escaped relegation in the penultimate week, and that was a miracle. The day that García had been presented as coach, arriving on a rescue mission that seemed impossible, the sporting director was overheard saying: “It’s like a funeral in here”.

DK Metcalf denies poking Cooper DeJean in the eyes after ejection from Pittsburgh Steelers-Philadelphia Eagles game
DK Metcalf was ejected from the Pittsburgh Steelers' 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday after two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties 10 offensive plays apart; the second of those appeared to see the receiver reach into Cooper DeJean's facemask and poke him in the eyes
Monday 23 November 2026 18:38, UK
Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf has denied intentionally poking Philadelphia Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean in the eyes after being ejected from the game during the second half of their 19-16 loss on Sunday.
Metcalf was tossed for the third time in his career after being flagged twice for personal fouls following a couple of confrontations with DeJean, the second of which included Metcalf appearing to stick his fingers in between the Eagles defender's facemask.
Asked on Monday if he could go into detail about his exchanges with DeJean, Metcalf initially responded that he "couldn't remember" before backtracking and saying that he was trying to send a message to DeJean to "stop pushing me".
Metcalf had caught only one pass for two yards before being sent to the locker room.
The 28-year-old was suspended for two games last season for swiping at a fan in Detroit and was shown the door twice earlier in his career while playing for the Seattle Seahawks.
Asked why this keeps happening, Metcalf told reporters: "I think you got to ask the people that seem to do that to me".
Metcalf noted that opponents trying to get under his skin is nothing new, saying that San Francisco 49ers players attempted to do that regularly during the Seahawks' frequent meetings with their NFC West rivals.
The two-time Pro Bowler, who is on pace for career lows in receptions and yards receiving this season, declined to blame the heated interaction on frustration, pointing out that the Steelers are "winning", though Pittsburgh (6-4) has dropped two straight after losing in Philadelphia.
Steelers coach Mike McCarthy called Metcalf's actions "unacceptable" but said he needed more information before deciding whether to take any action.
Metcalf did not appear to be worried about being disciplined by the Steelers or the NFL. "You've got to ask [Pittsburgh general manager] Omar [Khan] that, or anybody else other than DeKaylin," Metcalf said, using his given name.
The highest-paid wide receiver in team history also added that the Steelers need to "score points when we get the ball and not stall on third down or get a turnover on downs, stay on the field so our defense can stay off the field".
Pittsburgh remain firmly in playoff position as Thanksgiving looms but face a daunting stretch over the next three weeks that includes a pair of meeting with first-placed teams in their division - the Denver Broncos (8-2) and Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3), as well as a key clash with fellow AFC wildcard contenders the Houston Texans (4-6).

items.text:
We are proud to announce something that our small team of very dedicated people at Kagi has been building for a long time – the public beta of Kagi Mail. A private email and calendar with a @kagimail.com address, or with your own domains.
If you’ve already swapped Google Search for Kagi and Chrome for Orion, your inbox is probably the last big piece of your digital life still at Google. Now you can move that too.
Try Kagi Mail free for 60 days
$99/year (+ Sales Tax) after that. Included with Kagi Ultimate.
Why we built it
Does the world need another email service? We asked ourselves that question more than once. There are great ones out there, and we’re fans of what Fastmail and Tuta are doing. We still built our own, for the same reason we build everything at Kagi: technology should do its job and then get out of your way.
For email, that job is to be fast, private, and secure. On top of that, it should help you stay on track with what’s important: bring forward what you need to act on, respond to, or acknowledge, and quietly handle the rest.
Kagi Mail also has to treat you the way Kagi Search and Orion do: no surveillance, no ads, open standards, and no lock-in.
Already a Kagi member?
Kagi Mail is included in Ultimate. Sign in with your Kagi account, and you’re set. AI features draw from your existing Allowance. On another plan, or no Kagi account yet? After the free 60-day trial, you can get Kagi Mail for $99/year (+ Sales Tax).
How it works: A service and a client, on open standards
To deliver the experience we believe in, we built the full stack: hosting for your addresses and domains, plus the mail and calendar apps. It runs on open standards and open-source infrastructure (the Stalwart server, IMAP, JMAP, and CalDAV), so you can use Kagi’s apps or any compatible client you already like.
The basics
- A @kagimail.com address
- Unlimited aliases
- Unlimited domains
- Built-in Calendar
- 50 GB of storage
Intelligence
- Organize your mail in your own words. Brief it the way you’d brief an assistant: “Label anything where beta users send product feedback. It might come from @kagimail.com, but use judgment.” You decide what permissions each rule gets (read the content, or skip the inbox).
- Inbox Highlights show what needs you today, and learn from what you dismiss.
- Ask your inbox in plain language and get direct answers with the source email, including text inside scanned PDFs and photos.
- Newsletter view reads newsletters like a feed, out of the way of real mail.
- Responsible AI, with one switch to turn it all off. You control what AI is allowed to do and infer.
Private by default
- Tracking pixels and remote images are blocked or proxied, so senders can’t tell when or where you opened their mail.
- Sender screening holds new senders until you approve them, so they never reach your inbox uninvited.
- Suspicious senders trigger a phishing warning, while verified senders show their (BMI) logo.
No ads, ever. No profiling, no selling, no sharing your data.
For teams and families
- Shared addresses on your domain (team@, info@, family@): create an alias, then choose which people have access to it
- Sign in through a social login, or your organization’s own identity provider (OIDC)
- Coming soon: Shared mailboxes
Kagi integration
- Kagi Translate is built in
- Email Assistant: Write to assistant@kagimail.com for answers about your mail (actions coming soon)
- Proofread and translation included while you write emails
For power users and developers
- Keyboard-first: command palette, shortcuts, and search operators
- Rule-based filtering with Sieve, no AI involved
- MCP server with read access to your mail
- Works with Apple Mail, Thunderbird, and any IMAP/JMAP/CalDAV client, with automatic setup
What’s not here yet
We will keep adding new capabilities – here’s what to expect over the next few quarters.
Until the mobile apps arrive, use the mobile web app or any IMAP/JMAP client, such as Apple Mail or Thunderbird.
Our “no lock-in” promise to you
Leaving Kagi Mail is as easy as joining it. Your mail, calendar, and workflows are yours, and you can export them at any time, through standard protocols and a one-click export experience. You’ll keep access to your mailbox for six months after leaving Kagi Mail. You can send and receive emails for the first 60 days, then read and export your mail with one click for the remaining four months. We build an ecosystem so things work better together for those who want it, not to trap anyone.
Try Kagi Mail free for 60 days
$99/year (+ Sales Tax) after that. Included with Kagi Ultimate.
We want Kagi Mail to be the first email account we’d create for our children. We’re not there yet, but it is a high bar we hold ourselves to, and every feature in this beta is a step toward it: a calm, safe place to communicate, and a window onto an internet that treats you as a person, not a product who’s been tracked, targeted, and sold to.
We can build it this way because of you. Kagi has no ad business, and no one pushing us to monetize your inbox; you’re not a dataset for ads or AI. You are here because you believe the internet can be built differently. Thank you.

items.text:
Amazon has agreed to acquire a good chunk of Israeli startup Decart.
The e-commerce and cloud giant is paying $7.5 billion for the startup, according to Bloomberg.
Decart has made a name for itself building interactive real-time world models — most recently Oasis 3 — and AI video generation tools. But under the hood, the company stands out for its Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), software that helps AI models to run efficiently on Nvidia, Amazon, and Google’s hardware.
As part of the deal, Amazon will acquire the technology behind DOS, as well as Decart’s founding team and team of AI researchers and engineers, Amazon said in a blog post.
“Every leap forward in AI starts with getting more out of every chip,” said Peter DeSantis, SVP of foundational AI models, custom silicon, quantum computing, at Amazon. “More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost.”
Amazon, which has been so far been using its Trainium chips at its own data centers, is preparing to start selling them to customers as a competitor to Nvidia. Decart’s technology could make it easier for customers to run their workloads on Amazon chips, rather than Nvidia’s, which has been the gold standard so far.
Decart and Amazon did not immediately return requests for comment.

items.text:
'No-one's coming to save us' - but how can Man Utd save themselves?
- Published
Manchester United's Premier League trip to Anfield was described by some as a free hit for new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.
The theory was expectations for United were so low as they travelled to Liverpool that a positive outcome would be a huge bonus, and anything else was expected.
But Pochettino did not look like a man without pressure after 15 minutes of what turned into a 4-0 defeat.
By that point, his side were already 2-0 behind and down to 10 men. Liverpool's fans were gleefully singing about the Argentine being "sacked in the morning", even though he was only a sixth of the way through his first game in charge.
A day later, United supporters began filtering through Manchester Airport on their way to Lisbon for a Champions League match that marks the next stop in what has turned into a desperate campaign.
The prevailing mood was one of resigned acceptance punctuated by dark humour around what a season in the Championship might look like, and whether Manchester City might be there with them.
United's England midfielder Kobbie Mainoo summed the situation up when he spoke to MUTV after the final whistle at Anfield.
"We're at the lowest we've ever been and no-one's coming to save us," said the 21-year-old.
"There are no helping hands coming, so we've got to work together, lean on each other, keep working and hopefully it will come good.
"It's all about character now."
Tough tests before the transfer window opens
United are giving little away about their plans for the January transfer window.
Depending on finances, a striker and left-back are priorities but they still have nine games to play before they can make any changes to their squad. And even then, it is not certain to what extent it can happen.
Among those fixtures are home games against Coventry, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland.
Newly promoted Coventry are four points ahead of United, who are second from bottom. Forest and Sunderland are in the two positions immediately above the Old Trafford outfit.
A trip to Crystal Palace - the one side below United, and the other Premier League club to replace their coach during the international break - looms on 13 December.
After Wednesday's encounter with Sporting, Pochettino's side have one Champions League game before the end of the year - against RB Leipzig on 8 December.
Any solutions to be found to the current mess over the next five weeks have to come from within. If they don't, light-hearted discussions about a first relegation since 1973-74 under Tommy Docherty start to get serious.
"They have got enough in that squad to get themselves out of the bottom three," Ashley Young - a Premier League winner with United - told Match of the Day.
"They have not been showing that, but Pochettino has only just come in. He is going to want to get his team set up in a way that they are hard to beat. Right now, they do not look like they are hard to beat.
"It doesn't look like there is that togetherness. He has got to find a way to get that out of them. I am sure he will be able to do that when he has been longer in the job."
Fixing a leaky defence
Pochettino shut down a question about United's terrible recent defensive record when he spoke to the media immediately after the game at Anfield.
"Tell me only about the circumstance today," he said. "I wasn't [here] in the past."
That is true - and may also have been a useful diversion exercise in avoiding a dissection of a defensive unit he is still getting to know.
However, Pochettino knows United have kept one clean sheet all season - against Azerbaijani champions Sabah FK in September. He will also know United have now conceded 19 goals in their past six games.
Pochettino's big decision at Liverpool was to pick Matthijs de Ligt in the centre of a three-man defence ahead of Harry Maguire.
"He played in the Champions League you know, before the internationals," said the former Tottenham, PSG and Chelsea boss.
It was not clear when Pochettino meant.
In the 4-1 loss at Como on 21 October, De Ligt made his first appearance in 11 months following major back problems that eventually required surgery, largely because Leny Yoro was suspended and Lisandro Martinez was injured. He then played for two minutes against Roma on 3 November, when he was thrown on as then manager Michael Carrick searched desperately for a winner.
Most goals can be broken down into a number of mistakes that compound to make an eventual negative outcome.
Team positioning has been mentioned as a reason De Ligt found himself exposed under a high ball at Anfield. However, his failure to deal with it presented Alexander Isak with a clear run at goal and prompted Yoro to make the tackle that led to his controversial dismissal, which Pochettino felt shaped the 82 minutes that followed.
But United have been conceding bad goals all season. Numerous players have been culpable.
There is a limit to what Pochettino can do in the time available. However, he wants to maximise what he can do.
Whereas Carrick tended to let his starting players have a day off after matches, the new regime has decided a warm-down session at Carrington is the better option.
And defensive organisation was surely one of the key points his coaching team had on their list of things to work on when the players began preparations to face Sporting on Wednesday.
Will January be the answer Man Utd need?
With £70m summer arrival Carlos Baleba injured for the second time since the start of pre-season, Pochettino must find a way to protect United's goal, which might require additional support in midfield.
The strengths of Mainoo and Youri Tielemans are with the ball. Either with three in the middle of defence or a third man in midfield, a way needs to be found to stop opposition attacks running straight at the defence.

items.text:
Hibs boss Reedijk rejects talk of Easter Road jinx
- Published
Manager Marink Reedijk has rejected suggestions Easter Road is jinxed despite Hibernian being without a home win in the Scottish Premiership for more than seven months.
Hibs have lost nine of their last 10 home league games, with the 3-0 victory against Kilmarnock on 4 April under former manager David Gray the last success in the Premiership in front of their own fans.
Reedijk - in charge for seven matches, three of which have been at home - believes a focus on "brilliant basics" can end that dismal run on Tuesday night against Dundee, who conceded eight at home to Heart of Midlothian at the weekend.
"We need to be ourselves, need to show what we're capable of, show what we've worked at, who we are," said the Dutchman.
"On Saturday we didn't represent ourselves in that way. Therefore if we start to do these things well in a consistent manner, I don't see that anything is jinxed whatsoever. It's up to us."
The wretched sequence stretches back to the end of last season, when Hearts, Celtic and Motherwell won after the Premiership split and continued this season with the Steelmen and their Edinburgh rivals triumphing again at Easter Road.
Victories for Kilmarnock, Falkirk, Celtic and the mauling at the hands of Dundee United have been punctuated only by a draw against similarly out-of-form Aberdeen.
"The basics we've been doing well in the other matches, we didn't do them on Saturday. That was for me, I wouldn't say a shock but it was surprising," Reedijk added.
"Saturday didn't represent who we are and didn't represent the week's training we had. It is important you are consistent in the things you do.
"I keep repeating the word consistency and the basic things that make us good: being intense, being brave in trying to go forward, being on the front foot, being proactive and sticking together.
"For me the key is to do things consistently and to be happy to do the brilliant basics over and over and over again."
The Dens Park club might be ideal opponents for Hibs to be facing - the last Dundee manager to win in Leith was Ivano Bonetti more than a quarter of a century ago.

items.title: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson
items.summary: In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magn
items.text:
In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter.
Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0. Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023. Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered.
And when you’ve conceded more goals in all competitions this season than anybody else in Europe’s top five leagues, and when you’ve let in more in the league than anybody other than Crystal Palace, it’s pretty obvious that the defence is a major problem. There are serious reasons for concern; a switch of manager alone will not magically save United.
Perhaps Yoro was unfortunate to be sent off. Senne Lammens may have got to the ball ahead of Alexander Isak. But the opposite is also true. Had Yoro not been sent off, it would only have been because Isak’s first touch was heavy. By far the bigger issue as Pochettino prepares for Wednesday’s Champions League game at Sporting and Saturday’s Premier League match at home to Brentford is how easily United were undone by a simple ball over the top. First Matthijs de Ligt, who was much deeper than the rest of the defensive line, inexcusably left it, and then Yoro, in scrambling back, made an appallingly clumsy foul.
De Ligt, who has only been back in training for six weeks as he recovers from a back injury, had not started a league game since November last year. He looked way off the pace, as he had in the defeat to Como, and his selection, in retrospect, was an error by Pochettino. Yoro, who had looked one of United’s better recent signings in his first year after signing from Lille, had become a case study in the damage being part of a dysfunctional team can do to a player: his confidence is shot and he now lurches around like a sad horse, a player who seems always to be at the centre of unfortunate events – such as that header against his own bar against Aston Villa.
There are manifold problems at United, from the leadership to the recruitment to the stadium, but if there is to be an improvement in form, the first thing Pochettino needs to do is to change the mood. This is nothing like a great squad. It is a mess of ideas and strategies, put together over six different managers with no consistent goal in sight. But it is not a squad made up of terrible players. It is a squad made up of players who have lost their way, who had been dragged down into the morass. It’s obvious that United should be better than this, but even this United should be better than this.
United have won only one of 11 games in the league this season, and that was against newly-promoted Ipswich in August. To put that in context, Burnley are the only other side of all 92 in the league not to have won at least twice; when United were relegated in 1973-74, they won three of their first 11 games. Bruno Fernades has now played in four defeats to Liverpool by four goals or more, a record.
It remains, still, almost inconceivable that United will be relegated, or even that they will find themselves in a proper battle. It’s almost a category error; this cannot happen. But there are no terrible sides in the Premier League this season. Perhaps Manchester City’s appeal will fail and their punishment means they will obligingly occupy one of the relegation slots. But the three promoted sides are all showing signs of fight. Crystal Palace will probably improve under Thomas Frank, Sunderland have started keeping clean sheets and are a very different side if Brian Brobbey is fit, Nottingham Forest are far better than their league positions suggests and Fulham are five league games unbeaten.
A bounce will, surely, come at some point under Pochettino but, this season, nothing can be taken for granted at the bottom.

items.text:
Raya to miss Dortmund game but injury 'not serious'
- Published
Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya's shoulder injury "doesn't look too serious", but he will miss Tuesday's Champions League against Borussia Dortmund, says Mikel Arteta.
Raya was helped off the pitch in the 70th minute of Arsenal's 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Saturday.
He hurt his left shoulder while claiming a cross and making contact with Newcastle forward William Osula.
"We need some more tests [on Tuesday] but it is quite encouraging," said Gunners boss Arteta.
"He is not fit [to face Dortmund] but it doesn't look too serious."
Arteta said that while the incident looked pretty innocuous the pain his keeper was in made him fear it was a serious injury.
"With the pain that he was showing immediately after the action we were all quite worried but it seems to be better than what we expected," said Arteta.
"When you look at the action it doesn't seem to be much but the extent of the pain that he had and how he was struggling, it was quite worrying.
"We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had in that moment.
"The first tests that we have done have shown something that is much more encouraging. He does not need to have surgery which was the worry as that would rule him out for months so let's see."
- Raya set to have scan on injury - how much would Arsenal miss him? 
  - Published1 day ago
Arsenal face Borussia Dortmund, Manchester City, Brentford, Tottenham Hotspur and Real Madrid in their next tranche of matches.
And Raya is huge part of the way that Arsenal play because of his ability with the ball at his feet.
When asked if losing Raya for a long period of time would be the biggest blow to his team, Arteta said: "We have seen what David brings to the team but as well that is why we are very protective with Kepa [Arrizabalaga] and Illan [Meslier].
"Everybody needs to be ready because these things unfortunately happen and now we need to show everyone how well we are protected and the good keepers that we have in Kepa and Illan."

Mikel Arteta is hopeful the shoulder injury David Raya sustained at Newcastle is not too serious but confirmed the goalkeeper would miss Tuesday’s Champions League game against Borussia Dortmund.
Raya was forced off in the second half of Saturday’s 2-2 draw with a suspected dislocated shoulder, raising fears he could be sidelined for an extended period. He had an MRI scan on Arsenal’s return to London and was absent from training on Monday.
Kepa Arrizabalaga is expected to deputise at home to Dortmund but Arteta said Raya did not require surgery and could be in contention to face Manchester City on Sunday.
“He’s not fit for tomorrow, unfortunately, but it doesn’t look too serious,” the manager said. “We need some more tests tomorrow, but he’s quite encouraging. With the pain that he was showing immediately after the action, we were all quite worried, but he seems to be better than what we expected. There’s no need of surgery, which was the main fear, especially because I was worried about it for months.”
Asked whether Raya could play at home to City, Arteta said: “Tomorrow we’ll have more tests and we will know. I think we’ve seen what David brings to the team as well. That’s why we are very protective with Kepa and [third-choice] Illan [Meslier]. Everybody needs to be ready because these things unfortunately happen.”
Dortmund are a point behind Arsenal in the Champions League after three wins from their first four matches and Niko Kovac’s side lead Bayern Munich by two points at the top of the Bundesliga. Arteta said a youthful side expected to feature Jobe Bellingham – who was called up by England for the first time last week alongside his brother, Jude – would provide a real test before Real Madrid visit in a fortnight.
“I think you have to congratulate mum and dad for what they’ve done because it’s incredible,” Arteta said of facing the Bellingham brothers in successive Champions League matches. “When you look at the two of them and you put a different shirt on, it’s incredible. But two amazing footballers, what they’re doing is remarkable. So let’s give credit as well to the parents.”

The four
items.text:
UK to host 2035 Women's World Cup, Fifa confirms
- Published
England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will jointly host the 2035 Women's World Cup, Fifa has confirmed.
It will be the first time a football World Cup has been held in the United Kingdom since the men's tournament in 1966.
The four countries were the only bidders for the tournament, and were ratified as co-hosts at a specially arranged virtual meeting from Fifa's Zurich headquarters.
The tournament will consist of 104 matches contested by 48 teams over 39 days.
The 'All Together' bid included a proposal to use 19 venues, with 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland and two in Wales.
Monday's special meeting of Fifa's Congress also approved the joint bid by Mexico, the United States, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031 finals, which will be the first to feature 48 teams.
The news comes on the same day the UK government announced a vision for one million more girls to play, watch or be in leadership roles in sport by the time the tournament takes place.
- Hosting World Cup means decade of excitement - Weir 
  - Published1 hour ago
Where will matches be held in 2035?
England failed to win the right to host the men's World Cups in 2006 and 2018, and a proposed UK and Ireland bid for the 2030 tournament was abandoned.
But England and Scotland hosted matches at the men's Euros in 2021, and England staged the women's European Championship in 2022, which the Lionesses won.
England, Scotland, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland will jointly host the men's European Championship in 2028.
Mark Bullingham, chief executive of the Football Association, said: "Hosting Euro 2022 allowed us to change the game in our country, by creating a generation of aspirational role models and growing demand from women and girls to play.
"Hosting a World Cup would give us the chance to build on that across all four nations."
The English stadiums included in the 2035 bid are: Villa Park, The Amex, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Emirates Stadium, Selhurst Park, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Wembley, Etihad Stadium, St James' Park, the City Ground, the Stadium of Light and Old Trafford.
If Manchester United's proposed new Old Trafford stadium does not go ahead, it would still be considered in its current form.
Cardiff City Stadium and Principality Stadium are the two Welsh venues, with Easter Road in Edinburgh and Hampden Park in Glasgow in Scotland.
Northern Ireland missed out on co-hosting the men's Euros in 2028 after the UK government said in 2024 it would not provide funding to redevelop Casement Park in time - but a redeveloped Windsor Park is set to stage matches in 2035.
A further three stadiums could be added - Birmingham's new Powerhouse Stadium, Wrexham's redeveloped Racecourse Ground, and a potential new Chelsea ground - which would take the tournament to 16 cities and 22 venues.
Fifa is yet to decide whether all four co-hosts will qualify automatically.
Shaping the future of the game
The participation of women and girls in football has risen by 2.3m since the Women's European Championship was held in England in 2022.
However, women remain significantly underrepresented in leadership positions.
Only a quarter of chief executive, chair or performance director roles in major UK sports are held by women and only 12% of sports federations are led by a female.
Noel Mooney, the chief executive of the Football Association of Wales, said: "This is a proud day for Welsh football.
"We've put forward Wrexham and Cardiff as host cities, and it's exciting to think what a World Cup could bring to both cities and the communities around them.
"In Llunio Cymru - our 10-year strategy - we've set ourselves the ambition of reaching the knockout stages in 2035. Some of the players who could take us there are learning the game at clubs across Wales today. Our job is to make sure that wherever a girl grows up in Wales, she can find a team close to home, have a coach who helps her develop and see a route to the Cymru shirt."
Irish Football Association chief executive Patrick Nelson said the event "would be felt in every club and every age group, in every part of the country".
"Our young players would grow up having watched the best in the world play at home, and there is no substitute for that," he added.
Scottish Football Association chief executive Ian Maxwell said hosting the tournament would be "the most significant thing to happen to the women's and girls' game in Scotland".
He added: "The impact would go far beyond just the matches themselves. The level of investment into coaching, facilities and player pathways in the years beforehand will shape the future of the game for the generations to come."
Fifa's evaluation, published earlier this month, rated the bid 4.3 out of five. Its contractual framework was rated 'medium risk', and the document claimed "certain government guarantees contain material qualifications, particularly regarding tax and safety and security".
That is thought to refer to a lack of agreement over a request by Fifa for tax-free status for all football-related activities.
The bid evaluation said: "The bidder has submitted an extensive set of government support documents and contractual hosting agreements, demonstrating the commitment of the relevant authorities and stakeholders.
"However, certain government guarantees, particularly those relating to safety and security and tax, contain certain qualifications which have been duly noted in the legal evaluation.
"While certain contractual matters remain subject to further discussion, the bidder's proactive engagement with Fifa and the substantial lead-in time provide a sound basis for resolving these outstanding issues."

items.title: ‘Celebrate, inspire, unite’: UK confirmed as host of 2035 Women’s World Cup
items.summary:
The UK is to host the 2035 Women’s World Cup, Fifa has confirmed. England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will stage the first World Cup hosted in the country since the 1966 men’s tournament in England.
The UK bid was the only one under consideration for 2035. The 2031 tournament has been awar
items.text:
The UK is to host the 2035 Women’s World Cup, Fifa has confirmed. England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will stage the first World Cup hosted in the country since the 1966 men’s tournament in England.
The UK bid was the only one under consideration for 2035. The 2031 tournament has been awarded, also uncontested, to the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica. The decisions were formalised at a virtual meeting of Fifa’s national associations on Monday.
Debbie Hewitt, the Football Association chair, said of the 2035 World Cup: “Together we will celebrate the power of women’s football, inspire the next generation and unite fans from every corner of the world.”
The UK bid lists 22 stadiums as potential venues. Sixteen are in England, three in Wales, two in Scotland and one is in Northern Ireland. Fifteen host cities are in the running (the bid officially lists 16, counting Trafford as distinct from Manchester).
Andy Burnham said the tournament would bring “visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country”. The prime minister also pointed to the sporting impact, saying it would “bring more people into the game and leave a legacy that lasts long after the final whistle”.
Wembley has been proposed for the final, having hosted it at the 2022 Women’s European Championship. Fifa has evaluated 19 stadiums, assessing them as being of “high quality”. All were awarded an score of at least four out of five, except for Elland Road in Leeds (3.9), Easter Road in Edinburgh, Windsor Park in Belfast and Nottingham’s City Ground (all 3.6). Old Trafford has been assessed by Fifa but the proposed new Manchester United stadium could play a significant role instead if built in time.
The three listed stadiums not assessed by Fifa are Birmingham City’s proposed 62,000-seat Powerhouse Stadium, Wrexham’s stadium – which is due two stages of redevelopment – and Chelsea’s stadium because only a redeveloped Stamford Bridge or a new club stadium would come into the picture.
The 22 stadiums will be whittled down to between 14 and 16. The tournament is scheduled to involve 104 matches played by 48 teams over 39 days. The dates are yet to be confirmed but indicative dates of 21 June to 29 July have been informally used as a template during the bidding process.
The tournament is due to be the second Women’s World Cup to include 48 teams, after 2031’s event, mirroring this year’s men’s tournament and making it the largest single-sport event staged in the UK. There are to be 12 groups of four teams followed by knockouts starting with a last 32.
As revealed by the Guardian last week, Fifa is at loggerheads with the UK’s government and four football associations over the world governing body’s demands for tax-free status and exemptions from exchange-rate fees at the tournament.
England, Scotland and Wales are also due to co-host – along with the Republic of Ireland – the men’s European Championship in 2028.

The 2035 edition will be the second tournament featuring 48 nations, following 2031, which will be hosted by Costa Rica, Jamaica, Mexico and the United States, whose bid - which also ran unopposed - was also confirmed to be successful.
The dates for the tournament are yet to be confirmed.
It will take place across 19 stadiums across 15 cities, with one additional host city and three additional stadiums for future consideration.
Presenting the bid at the FIFA meeting, Sky Sports News presenter - and non-executive FA director - Jess Creighton said: "Welcome to your Women's World Cup 2035. A tournament where we want every team, every fan and every nation to feel at home.
"Across the UK, football has always been about bringing people together - and that's why, in 2035, we'll welcome it the way football always has: by helping everyone feel at home.
"Our ambition is to deliver the most-watched FIFA Women's World Cup ever.
"We're predicting in 2035, there will be more than 3.5bn viewers, and over 4.5m tickets sold."
English Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt addressed the Congress after the bid's success had been confirmed.
"Thank you for your trust and confidence in awarding us the FIFA Women's World Cup 2035," Hewitt said.
"We're deeply honoured by your support and grateful for the opportunity to host the pinnacle of women's football on behalf of the global football family.
"As we said throughout our bid, we want this to be your FIFA Women's World Cup, a World Cup for everyone.
"Together, we will celebrate the power of women's football, inspire the next generation, and unite fans from every corner of the world. We look forward to welcoming you to the United Kingdom in 2035 and just as importantly, to working closely with you all in the years ahead to deliver an exceptional FIFA Women's World Cup that the entire football community can be proud of."
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: "The world is coming to the United Kingdom. In 2035 the biggest tournament in women's sport will be played in cities across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, bringing visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country.
"Our players have inspired a generation of girls. In 2035 that generation will watch the best in the world play on their doorstep - and some of them will be on the pitch. But the impact of this World Cup will go much further. It will reach into communities across the country, bring more people into the game and leave a legacy that lasts long after the final whistle."

Carlos Alcaraz: Spaniard is 'toughest player to play against' right now with Jannik Sinner out of the equation, says Tim Henman
Carlos Alcaraz will head into the 2027 season as the player to beat with Italian Jannik Sinner currently missing from the ATP Tour due to a knee injury; You can watch the Next Gen ATP Finals from 9-13 December in Reggio Calabria, Italy live on Sky Sports Tennis
Monday 23 November 2026 15:20, UK
Carlos Alcaraz is the "toughest player to play against" right now with Jannik Sinner out of the equation, says Tim Henman.
Alcaraz began the year facing questions over his split with long-time coach Juan Carlos Ferrero, but the Spaniard has answered them emphatically by completing the career Grand Slam and adding the elusive ATP Finals title to his collection.
Since returning at the US Open in late August, the 23-year-old has made up for lost time in a superb late-season charge that culminated in Sunday's triumph in Turin, where he beat top-ranked Alexander Zverev in the final.
- Keep track of the full tennis schedule live on Sky Sports
- Download Sky Sports app for analysis, news and video 📺
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract on NOW📱
By winning the ATP Tour's season-ender, Alcaraz joined Andre Agassi, Roger Federer and Novak Djokovic as the only men to secure the career Grand Slam and ATP Finals title.
With former world No 1 Jannik Sinner set to undergo surgery on a persistent knee injury in Finland this week, casting doubt over his participation in the Australian Open, Alcaraz looks set to dominate tennis in 2027.
Speaking at the ATP Finals in Turin, former British No 1 Henman told Sky Sports Tennis: "We can obviously have a deep dive into the five matches here, but I think in the context of being out of the game for four and a half months, that is not easy then to come back into a Grand Slam.
"He played well in New York, getting through to the quarter-finals, but then we just have to look at this last third of the season.
"For him to not lose a match, play a couple of matches at Laver Cup, and then he's gone on this tear where every aspect of his game has been so impressive. The physical side of things, the wrist has obviously been perfect.
"Yes, he had a challenge with the hamstring, but mentally and technically his game has been so good. In Paris, he didn't have it all his own way, and I think that was such a good sign that he can play and win with this sort of B or C game.
"He's now come into the Tour-ending championships, the best against the best, an event that he's never won, and he's taken the title."
Henman: A completely different level
Four of the Spaniard's six titles this year have come since he returned from injury, with triumphs in Tokyo and Vienna followed by victories at the Paris Masters and the ATP Finals - all under the guidance of head coach Samuel Lopez and brother Alvaro.
"He started the year off with a bang down in Australia, that was the one Grand Slam that he was missing from his CV," Henman said.
"To be able to achieve the career Grand Slam at such a young age was incredible.
"Then obviously on to the clay, getting injured in Barcelona, missing a big chunk, missing two slams at Roland-Garros and Wimbledon, coming back in New York.
"Zverev's got a better serve than Alcaraz, and he hadn't lost his serve. This is the skill set and the challenge of playing Alcaraz, and I think he's in Zverev's head, obviously, because it was just a completely different level.
"Zverev couldn't find the spots, and then his serve has been unbreakable by everyone else in the tournament, and Alcaraz has dismantled him."
Alcaraz is 'the best'
Former doubles No 1 Jamie Murray said: "He [Alcaraz] is amazing. He is the best. He plays in a completely different way to anything that we see these days on the ATP Tour.
"He obviously came back at the US Open, it's not an easy thing to do. I'm sure he was disappointed losing to [Ben] Shelton, the way that he went out there, but it definitely helped him after that for the rest of the year.
"He was up to speed, he had his rhythm. It's not a huge surprise, because he is one of the two best players in the world, and his level is so much better than everybody else when he's in full flow.
"It's an amazing run that he's won these last three tournaments, but it's not out of the realm of possibility for Carlos Alcaraz to do that."
